Common Types & Use Cases

·       Heirloom antique necklace - same per-gram rate as new gold

·       Vintage Mughal/Nizami antique necklace - heritage value not paid

·       Antique temple necklace with stones - stones removed, gold weight only

·       Antique pendant with antique chain - weighed separately or together

·       Damaged/discoloured antique - condition does not affect resale value

Resale Value & Worked Example

The antique factor adds no resale premium. For a 30g 22K antique necklace: 30 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹4,19,070.

For a 60g heavy antique: ₹8,38,140. If you have an antique piece with significant historical value (e.g. a documented royal piece), an auction house may offer more than gold weight; but at a standard gold buyer, only the gold content is paid.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is an antique gold necklace worth at a gold buyer?

Only gold weight and purity are paid. A 30g 22K antique necklace is worth ₹4,19,070 - the same as a new 30g 22K necklace.

Why doesn't age add value at a gold buyer?

A gold buyer melts/recycles gold. The market price is based on the raw gold content. Antique value (design, craftsmanship, heritage) is paid only by collectors or auction houses, not commodity gold buyers.

Should I sell my heirloom antique necklace at an auction house instead?

If the piece has documented heritage or significant artistic merit, an auction or antique jewellery specialist may pay above gold value. For pieces without such provenance, gold buyers typically offer competitive cash payment.

How is antique gold tested for purity?

XRF (X-ray fluorescence) at the branch - same as modern gold. Older antique pieces may be 20K or 22K, occasionally 18K. XRF accurately measures any purity.

Are stones in antique necklaces valued?

No. Stones are removed and returned. Only the gold weight is paid.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 - most antique necklaces above 16g cross this.

Can I sell a damaged or broken antique necklace?

Yes. Physical condition does not affect gold purity. Even broken antique pieces are paid at the full per-gram rate.

·       Selling complete stack vs individual rings - both options

Each ring in a stack is weighed individually. For a stack of 3 rings totalling 5g of 22K gold: 5 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹69,845.

How much is a gold stackable ring worth today?

What is a stackable ring?

A stackable (or stack) ring is a thin gold band designed to be worn together with other thin rings on the same finger for a layered fashion look.

Can I sell just one ring from a stack?

What if my stack contains mixed gold purities?

Each ring is XRF-tested individually. A 22K ring is paid at the 22K rate; an 18K ring at the 18K rate.

Most modern stack rings are 18K or 14K (more durable for thin designs). Some are 22K. XRF confirms each.

The gold band is paid by weight; small diamond accents are typically removed and returned (too small for separate valuation).

html:
A designer gold chain is an ornate, artistic chain featuring intricate craftsmanship, often handcrafted with traditional motifs (peacocks, paisleys, floral patterns) or modern artistic designs. Designer chains can be from named designers (Tanishq, Bhima, PC Jeweller) or independent goldsmiths.

At resale, the designer craftsmanship adds no premium - only gold weight and purity determine cash value. This is important to understand: you do not recover the design premium paid at purchase.

At a Glance

Common Types & Use Cases

·       Handcrafted traditional motif chain (peacock, paisley) - 8g–30g

·       Brand designer chain (Tanishq, Bhima, etc.) - same rate as plain

·       Modern artistic designer chain - craftsmanship not paid at resale

·       Stone-set designer chain - stones removed at resale

·       Custom-made designer chain - same per-gram rate as factory chain

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 20g 22K designer chain: 20 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,79,380.

For a 35g heavy designer piece: ₹4,88,915. Important: if you paid ₹1,80,000 for a 20g designer chain (gold + making charges + GST), you receive only ₹2,79,380 at resale. Making charges do not return.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold designer chain worth today?

A 20g 22K designer chain is worth ₹2,79,380. The designer/brand premium adds no resale value.

Why doesn't designer craftsmanship add value at resale?

Gold buyers melt or recycle gold; the market price is for raw gold content. Designer premium is paid only by buyers wanting the specific design, not by commodity gold buyers.

Do branded chains (Tanishq, Bhima) fetch more?

At a gold buyer, no. The brand does not add resale value. Hallmarking matters (it confirms purity), but the brand name itself does not add to the per-gram rate.

Should I sell my designer chain through the original jeweller?

Many branded jewellers offer exchange schemes where you can use the value toward a new purchase. The cash value is typically the same as a gold buyer offers. Exchange is convenient but not financially superior.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What purity are designer chains?

Most are 22K (916). Some modern designer pieces are 18K. XRF confirms.

How are stones in a designer chain handled?

Removed before weighing. All stones returned. Only gold portion paid.

How the Gold Resale Calculator Works

The gold resale value formula is: Cash Value = Weight (grams) × Purity Fraction × Today's 24K IBJA Rate.

The purity fraction converts your karat into a decimal: 24K = 1.000, 22K = 0.916, 18K = 0.750, 14K = 0.585.

Gold purity determines exactly how much of your jewellery is actual gold - and therefore how much cash you receive when you sell. Understanding the gold purity chart is the single most important step before selling any gold ornament.

This guide explains every purity level, the BIS hallmark codes on your jewellery and how purity directly impacts your resale value.

At a Glance

22K gold purity

How to Find Your Gold's Purity

·       BIS hallmark on your jewellery - look for the 6-digit HUID and the purity code (916, 750, etc.)

·       XRF (X-ray fluorescence) test - the most accurate method; takes 30 seconds at the branch

·       Acid test - older method; less common now that XRF is standard

·       Stamping alone - not always reliable; XRF gives the final definitive reading

How Purity Affects Your Resale Value

A 10g necklace at 22K yields ₹1,39,690 today. The same 10g piece at 18K yields ₹1,14,375 - a difference of ₹25,315. Knowing your purity before selling prevents being underpaid.

Formula: Cash Value = Weight (g) × (Purity / 24) × Today's 24K Rate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the purity of 22K gold?

22K gold is 91.6% pure gold - it has 22 parts gold and 2 parts alloying metals (usually copper and silver for strength). The BIS hallmark code is 916.

How do I check gold purity at home?

The most reliable way is to visit a gold buyer or jeweller for XRF testing. At home, look for BIS hallmarks stamped on the jewellery (916 = 22K, 750 = 18K, 999 = 24K).

Is 22K or 24K gold better for resale?

24K gold gives a higher per-gram payout (since it is 100% gold), but most Indian jewellery is 22K. At resale, each is paid at the correct rate for its actual purity as tested by XRF.

What does the BIS hallmark mean?

BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) hallmark certifies gold purity. The 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) on BIS-hallmarked jewellery allows you to verify purity via the BIS Care app.

Can the acid test prove my gold is 22K?

Why does my antique jewellery test at 20K?

Older jewellery was often made to traditional standards (20K or 21K) before BIS hallmarking became standard. This is common and expected.

Does a higher karat mean more durable jewellery?

No - higher karat (more pure gold) is actually softer. 24K pure gold is the softest; 18K and 14K are more durable because of alloying metals. For resale, higher purity gives a higher per-gram rate.

source.title: Gold Bajuband - Upper Arm Ornament Resale Value

html:
A bajuband (also spelled bajubandh, bahubandh or armlet) is a gold ornament worn on the upper arm, just above the elbow. It is one of the oldest pieces of Indian jewellery, worn by brides across North India, Rajasthan and South India (where it is called vanki). Bajubands range from simple plain bands to elaborate stone-set bridal pieces.

At resale, only the gold weight and purity determine cash value. Stones and embellishments are handled separately.

At a Glance

Standard bajuband

15g – 30g gold

Heavy bridal bajuband

Common Types & Use Cases

·       Standard bajuband - festive/wedding upper arm piece, 15g–30g

·       Heavy bridal bajuband - elaborate stone-set design, 25g–50g

·       Vanki (South Indian) - same ornament, regional name; same per-gram rate

·       Heirloom bajuband - age adds no resale premium; gold weight only paid

·       Damaged/bent bajuband - condition does not affect purity or resale value

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 20g 22K bajuband: 20 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,79,380.

For a heavy 35g bridal bajuband: ₹4,88,915. Note: vanki (South Indian variant) is valued identically.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold bajuband worth today?

A 20g 22K bajuband is worth ₹2,79,380. A 35g heavy piece brings ₹4,88,915.

What is the difference between bajuband and vanki?

Bajuband is the North Indian/Hindi term; vanki is the South Indian (Telugu/Tamil/Kannada) term for the same upper-arm ornament. Both are valued identically by gold weight and purity.

Are stones in a bajuband paid at resale?

No. Stones are removed before weighing and returned to you. Only the gold portion is paid.

What documents do I need?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 - standard bajubands above ~14g cross this.

What purity are bajubands?

Most are 22K. Some traditional/older pieces may be 20K. XRF at the branch confirms.

Can I sell a single bajuband?

Yes. Bajubands are typically sold as a pair but individual pieces are accepted.

Is this the same as an armlet?

Yes. Bajuband, bahubandh, vanki and armlet all refer to upper-arm ornaments.

source.title: Gold Acid Test - How XRF & Acid Testing Works

html:
Before paying you for your gold, a buyer must confirm the exact purity of your piece. There are two main methods: the acid test (traditional) and XRF machine testing (modern standard). Understanding both helps you know what to expect and ensures you are not underpaid.

At a Glance

Acid test accuracy

~±2–3K (approximate)

XRF test accuracy

±0.1% (very precise)

Time for XRF test

30–60 seconds per piece

Damages your jewellery?

Acid: minor scratch / XRF: none

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is the Gold Acid Test?

The acid test uses nitric acid to check gold purity. A small scratch is made on a touchstone, the metal is rubbed on it, and acid is applied. The colour reaction indicates the approximate karat: 24K resists, lower karats show reactions.

The acid test is a rough guide - it can indicate purity within a range (e.g., 18K–22K) but cannot pinpoint exactly 91.6% vs 88% purity. It can also slightly damage the surface of your jewellery.

What Is XRF Testing?

Acid Test vs XRF - Comparison

Factor

Acid Test

XRF Test

Accuracy

±2–3K approximate

±0.1% precise

Damage to jewellery

Minor surface scratch

None (non-destructive)

Time

2–5 minutes

30–60 seconds

Result format

Visual colour range

Exact % composition

Can detect plating?

Limited

Yes - detects plated surfaces

Industry standard (2026)

Declining

Yes - universally adopted

What to Do If a Buyer Only Uses Acid Testing

·       Ask why XRF is not being used - reputable buyers use XRF

·       Acid tests can understate purity - you may receive less than you deserve

·       Request a second opinion at an XRF-equipped buyer before accepting

Can You Test Gold at Home?

Home testing kits (magnet test, acid kits, electronic testers) exist but are not reliable for determining exact purity for resale. A magnet test only confirms whether something is not gold (magnets attract iron/steel, not gold). Home electronic testers have poor accuracy.

For resale purposes, only an XRF test at a reputable buyer gives the definitive purity reading.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the acid test still used to buy gold?

Can acid testing damage my jewellery?

Yes - a small scratch is made on a touchstone. The scratch is minor but present. XRF requires no scratching.

How accurate is the XRF test?

XRF is accurate to ±0.1% purity - it gives the exact elemental composition of your gold piece.

Can XRF detect gold plating?

Yes. XRF can detect a thin gold layer over a base metal - it will show a thin gold reading over copper or silver. This distinguishes solid gold from gold-plated items.

What if I test my gold at home with a kit?

Home kits (acid kits, electronic testers) are not reliable for exact purity. For resale, always use XRF at a professional buyer.

How long does XRF testing take?

30–60 seconds per piece. For multiple pieces, testing is done one at a time and typically takes 5–15 minutes total.

html:
A gold charm bracelet is a chain bracelet adorned with multiple small decorative charms - animals, letters, religious symbols, hearts or other motifs - suspended from the links. The charms themselves are also gold (or a mix of gold and other metals), making the total weight a combination of the chain and all charms.

At resale, every component - chain and each charm - is weighed together. Only the total gold weight and purity are paid. The sentimental or decorative value of charms adds no premium.

At a Glance

Standard charm bracelet

Common Types & Use Cases

·       Light charm bracelet - 4g–10g, few charms added

·       Standard charm bracelet - 8g–18g, multiple small charms

·       Heavy charm-loaded bracelet - 15g–30g, many large charms

·       Mixed-metal charm bracelet - only gold charms/chain paid

·       Heirloom charm bracelet - sentimental value adds no resale premium

Resale Value & Worked Example

All gold components (chain + gold charms) are weighed together. For a 10g 22K charm bracelet: 10 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,39,690.

Non-gold charms (silver, base metal, enamel, resin) are removed and returned. Only the confirmed gold weight is paid.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold charm bracelet worth today?

A 10g 22K charm bracelet is worth ₹1,39,690. A 18g heavy piece brings ₹2,51,442.

Are all charms on a bracelet paid as gold?

Only gold charms are paid as gold. Non-gold charms (silver, brass, resin) are removed and returned. XRF testing confirms which charms are gold.

Is the sentimental value of charms paid?

No. Gold buyers pay only for the gold content. Sentimental value, brand value (e.g. Pandora gold charms) and craftsmanship are not paid.

Can I keep some charms and sell the rest?

Yes. Individual charms can be removed and weighed separately. You decide which pieces to sell.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Most charm bracelets are below ₹2,00,000 PAN threshold.

What purity are gold charm bracelets?

Most are 22K. Some modern charm bracelets use 18K. XRF tests each component.

How are mixed-metal charms handled?

Non-gold charms are removed before weighing and returned to you.

source.title: Gold Tennis Bracelet - Resale Value Guide

html:
A gold tennis bracelet is a flexible in-line bracelet featuring a continuous row of identically set diamonds or gemstones on a slim gold chain. The name comes from a 1987 US Open incident where tennis player Chris Evert's diamond bracelet snapped on court.

At resale, the gold chain and the diamonds are valued separately - the gold by weight and purity, the diamonds by certification.

At a Glance

5g – 10g gold

Standard tennis bracelet

8g – 16g gold

Heavy tennis bracelet

14g – 25g gold

Diamonds

Valued separately

₹1,39,690

Last Updated

May 2026

Live Rate Today

At today's IBJA rate of ₹15,250 per gram for 24K, a 22K piece yields ₹13,965 per gram.

Common Types & Use Cases

·       Classic diamond tennis bracelet - thin chain, 5g–10g gold

·       Standard tennis bracelet - 8g–16g gold chain with set diamonds

·       Heavy tennis bracelet - 14g–25g gold, larger diamonds

·       Coloured gemstone tennis bracelet - rubies/sapphires, same gold rate

·       18K white gold tennis bracelet - valued at 18K rate (0.75 × weight)

Resale Value & Worked Example

The gold chain is weighed after the diamonds are removed. For a 10g 22K gold chain: 10 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,39,690.

For an 18K white gold chain (10g): 10 × 0.75 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,14,375. Diamonds need separate certificate-based valuation - a gold buyer pays only for the gold portion.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold tennis bracelet worth at a gold buyer?

The gold chain portion: a 10g 22K chain is worth ₹1,39,690. Diamonds need separate valuation.

Are diamonds in a tennis bracelet paid at a gold buyer?

No. A gold buyer pays only for the gold chain. Diamonds require separate GIA/IGI certificate-based valuation.

Are most tennis bracelets 18K or 22K?

Most tennis bracelets use 18K gold (for durability to hold diamond settings). 18K is paid at ₹11,438/g today.

How are diamonds removed from a tennis bracelet?

At the branch, diamonds are carefully removed from each setting. All diamonds returned to you.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory for the gold sale. A GIA/IGI certificate for diamonds helps their separate valuation.

Can I sell the gold and keep the diamonds?

Yes. The diamonds are removed and returned. You receive the gold chain weight × purity rate.

How long to sell?

25–40 minutes including diamond removal, XRF testing and payment.

source.title: How to Sell Gold Without Receipt or Bill

keywords.keyword: how to sell gold without receipt

html:
Many people worry that they cannot sell gold jewellery without the original purchase bill or receipt. This is a common misconception. In India, you can legally sell gold without a purchase receipt - purity is determined by XRF machine testing, not by the original invoice.

You do need valid KYC documents (Aadhaar, and PAN if the sale exceeds ₹2,00,000). This guide explains everything.

At a Glance

Can you sell without receipt?

Yes - legally permitted

Purity determined by

XRF machine test at branch

Document required (all sales)

Aadhaar card

Document required (>₹2L)

PAN card

Original bill required?

No

KYC verification

Mandatory - Aadhaar + PAN if >₹2L

Last Updated

May 2026

Why No Receipt Is Needed

Gold is a commodity. Its value is determined by weight and purity - not by who sold it to you or when. An XRF machine tests the exact metal composition of your piece in 30–60 seconds, providing an accurate purity reading independent of any paperwork.

The original purchase bill is relevant for income tax purposes (proving your cost of acquisition for LTCG calculation), but it is not required to sell your gold at a gold buyer.

What You DO Need (KYC)

Document

When Required

Why

Aadhaar Card

All gold sales

Mandatory KYC - Prevention of Money Laundering Act

PAN Card

Sales above ₹2,00,000

Income Tax Act Section 114B

Original purchase bill

Not required for sale

Useful only for your own LTCG tax calculation

Hallmark certificate

Not required

XRF confirms purity independently

What Happens Without a Receipt

·       XRF test determines purity - accurate to ±0.1%

·       Weight is measured on calibrated scales

·       You receive the IBJA rate × weight × purity fraction

·       No deduction for missing receipt

·       Signed receipt is issued to you by the buyer after the sale

Impact on Your Tax Calculation

Without the original purchase bill, you may not be able to prove your cost of acquisition to the Income Tax Department. This matters if you are computing LTCG (Long Term Capital Gains) on the sale.

If you cannot prove the purchase price, the IT Department may treat the entire sale proceeds as capital gains. Consult a tax advisor if your sale value is significant.

Common Situations

·       Inherited gold - no receipt; sell freely with Aadhaar + PAN

·       Gift gold - no receipt; sell freely with KYC

·       Very old jewellery - no receipt; sell freely with KYC

·       Lost receipt - no issue for sale; may affect LTCG calculation

·       Hallmark missing - XRF still determines purity accurately

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold without the original bill in India?

Yes. Gold can legally be sold without the original purchase bill. XRF testing determines purity; Aadhaar and PAN are the only documents required.

What documents are required to sell gold?

Aadhaar is mandatory for all sales. PAN is required if the total sale amount exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What if my gold has no hallmark?

No hallmark is fine - XRF testing determines exact purity regardless of hallmarking status.

Can I sell inherited gold without a receipt?

Yes. Inherited gold is sold with Aadhaar (and PAN if above ₹2L). No purchase bill is required.

Will I be taxed on gold I sell without a receipt?

LTCG tax applies if you held the gold over 24 months. Without a purchase bill, proving your original cost basis is difficult - consult a tax advisor.

Does selling without a receipt mean I get less money?

No. The payout is entirely based on XRF-tested purity × weight × today's IBJA rate. Missing receipt does not reduce your payout.

What if the buyer asks for the original bill?

Reputable buyers do not require the original purchase bill. If a buyer insists, it may be a pretext for offering a lower price - visit a different buyer.

A gold collar necklace is a stiff, wide band that sits close to the neck - similar to a shirt collar. It is a bold statement piece at the crossover of traditional Indian chokers and modern Western jewellery design. Gold collar necklaces range from 12g to 50g+ depending on width and construction.

At resale, only gold weight and purity determine cash value.

·       Stone-set collar - diamonds/coloured stones removed at resale

·       Tribal/ethnic collar - same per-gram rate regardless of origin

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 25g 22K collar necklace: 25 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹3,49,225.

For a heavy 40g collar: ₹5,58,760. All collar necklace sales exceed ₹2,00,000 - Aadhaar and PAN both required.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold collar necklace worth today?

A 25g 22K collar is worth ₹3,49,225. A heavy 40g piece brings ₹5,58,760.

What is the difference between a collar and a choker?

A choker is typically a flexible, soft-fitting close necklace. A collar is a stiffer, wider band that holds its circular shape. Both are valued at the same per-gram rate.

Do I need PAN to sell a collar necklace?

Yes - virtually all collar necklaces exceed ₹2,00,000 at today's rates. Aadhaar and PAN are both required.

Are stones in a collar necklace paid?

No. Stones removed and returned. Only gold weight paid.

What documents?

Aadhaar and PAN (mandatory for this value range).

What purity are collar necklaces?

Most are 22K. Some modern designs use 18K. XRF confirms.

How long to sell?

25–40 minutes including XRF, weighing and payment.

A tassel earring has multiple thin gold chains/strands hanging together from a central element - resembling a decorative tassel or fringe.

All gold strands are weighed together as one total weight. No individual strand measurement is needed.

No. Stones/pearls removed before weighing and returned.

Aadhaar mandatory. Most tassel pairs below ₹2L PAN threshold.

Most are 22K. Some use 18K for the finer strands. XRF confirms.

Yes. Individual pieces are accepted.

·       Thin daily-wear anchor chain - 4g–10g

·       Standard anchor chain - 8g–20g, men or women

·       Heavy anchor chain - 15g–35g, statement piece

·       Anchor Chain with pendant - chain and pendant weighed together

·       Selling chain only (keeping pendant) - chain weighed alone

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 12g 22K anchor chain: 12 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,67,628.

For a 22g chain: ₹3,07,318. Chains above ~16g may exceed ₹2,00,000 - bring PAN.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold anchor chain worth today?

A 12g 22K anchor chain is worth ₹1,67,628. A 22g chain brings ₹3,07,318.

Does a anchor chain fetch more than other chain styles?

No. All chain styles are valued at the same per-gram IBJA rate. Link pattern is cosmetic.

Can I sell a damaged chain?

Yes. Physical damage does not affect gold purity.

Can I sell chain only (without pendant)?

Yes - weighed separately.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What purity are anchor chains?

Most are 22K. Lighter chains may be 18K. XRF confirms.

How long to sell?

source.title: Gold Eternity Ring - Resale Value Guide

html:
A gold eternity ring features a continuous row of identically set gemstones (usually diamonds) running around the entire band (full eternity) or halfway around (half eternity). Eternity rings are typically gifted as anniversary rings.

At resale, the gold band and the diamonds are valued separately - the gold by weight and purity, the diamonds by certification.

At a Glance

Full eternity ring (gold portion)

Last Updated

Common Types & Use Cases

·       Half eternity ring - diamonds halfway, 2g–5g gold

·       Full eternity ring - diamonds all around, 4g–10g gold

·       Diamond eternity ring - gold band paid, diamonds separately

·       Coloured stone eternity - rubies/sapphires, same gold rate

·       18K white gold eternity - valued at 18K rate (0.75 purity)

Resale Value & Worked Example

The gold band is weighed after diamonds are removed. For a 4g 22K band: 4 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹55,876. For a 7g full eternity 18K band: ₹80,062.

Diamonds need separate GIA/IGI certificate-based valuation at a diamond specialist.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold eternity ring worth at a gold buyer?

The gold band: a 4g 22K band is worth ₹55,876. A 7g 18K band is worth ₹80,062. Diamonds require separate valuation.

Are diamonds in an eternity ring paid at a gold buyer?

No. A gold buyer pays only for the gold band. Diamonds are removed and returned.

Is an eternity ring usually 18K or 22K?

Most eternity rings use 18K gold for durability to hold diamond settings. Some Indian eternity rings use 22K.

How are diamonds removed from an eternity ring?

At the branch, diamonds are removed from each setting and returned to you as loose stones.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Most eternity rings below ₹2L PAN threshold.

Can I sell just the gold band?

Yes. Diamonds returned; you receive the gold weight × purity rate.

Is a half eternity ring worth more than a full?

The gold band weight is what matters. A full eternity ring has more gold (running all around), so may yield slightly more for the gold portion.

·       Broad ornate pinky ring - statement piece, 4g–8g

·       Men's pinky ring with stone - stone removed at resale

·       Kids' little finger ring - same per-gram rate

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 3g 22K pinky ring: 3 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹41,907.

For a 6g broad piece: ₹83,814. Pinky rings are typically the lightest gold rings - most are well below the ₹2,00,000 PAN threshold.

What to Watch For

·       Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·       Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·       No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·       Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

How much is a gold pinky ring worth today?

A 3g 22K pinky ring is worth ₹41,907. A 6g piece brings ₹83,814.

Is a pinky ring valued differently from other rings?

No. All rings are valued at the same per-gram rate. The finger it is worn on does not affect the rate.

Can I sell a child's pinky ring?

Yes. Small children's rings are accepted. Even rings under 1g are weighed precisely on calibrated scales.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Pinky rings are typically well below ₹2L PAN threshold.

What purity are pinky rings?

Most are 22K. Some modern designs use 18K. XRF confirms.

Are stones in a pinky ring paid?

No. Stones removed and returned. Only gold portion paid.

How long to sell?

10–15 minutes - pinky rings are quick to test and weigh.

The mangalsutra chain is the gold chain component of the mangalsutra - the part that carries the black beads or holds the pendant. When selling a mangalsutra, the chain is often the component with the most gold weight. Many sellers choose to sell just the chain (keeping the pendant separately).

At resale, only the gold content of the chain is paid. Black beads interspersed in the chain are removed and excluded from the weight.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

Can I sell just the chain and keep the pendant?

Yes. Chain and pendant are weighed separately. You can sell one or both.

What is the difference between a mangalsutra chain and a regular gold chain?

A mangalsutra chain is specifically the chain forming part of a mangalsutra (may carry black beads). At resale, it is valued identically to any other gold chain - by weight and purity.

A tola is a traditional Indian unit of gold weight equal to 11.6638 grams. The tola was the standard weight for gold in the Indian subcontinent before metrication and is still widely used in North India, Pakistan and parts of the Gulf region.

Knowing the gold rate per tola helps sellers who have inherited gold described in tolas or those dealing with older jewellery receipts that list tola weights.

What Is a Tola?

A tola (also spelled 'tole' or 'tolah') is a traditional South Asian unit of gold weight. 1 tola = 11.6638 grams. It was the standard unit used by British India for gold transactions and remains in common use today for quoting gold prices in North India, Pakistan, Nepal and parts of the Gulf.

In South India, the equivalent unit is the pavan/sovereign (8 grams). The tola is approximately 1.46 pavans.

1 tola = 11.6638 grams. This is the standard conversion used in India and internationally.

source.title: Gold Men's Chain Bracelet - Resale Value

html:
A men's gold chain bracelet is a wrist bracelet with a chain-link design - distinct from a kada (solid bangle) or cuff (open band). Chain bracelets are popular among Indian men for both daily wear and formal occasions, coming in styles like curb-link, rope, figaro and flat-link.

At resale, only gold weight and purity determine cash value - the chain style and link pattern add no premium.

At a Glance

Thin chain bracelet

8g – 18g

Standard chain bracelet

15g – 30g

Heavy statement chain

25g – 50g

May 2026

Live Rate Today

Common Types & Use Cases

  • Thin curb-link chain bracelet - 8g–18g, daily men's wear
  • Standard rope/figaro chain bracelet - 15g–30g
  • Heavy Cuban/thick chain bracelet - 25g–50g, statement piece
  • Chain bracelet with ID plate - plate weight included
  • Heirloom men's chain bracelet - same per-gram rate as new

Resale Value & Worked Example

For an 18g 22K men's chain bracelet: 18 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,51,442.

For a heavy 35g Cuban-style bracelet: ₹4,88,915. Link pattern (curb, rope, figaro) adds no premium - only the gold weight is paid.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing
  • Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing
  • No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement
  • Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold men's chain bracelet worth today?

An 18g 22K chain bracelet is worth ₹2,51,442. A 35g heavy piece brings ₹4,88,915.

Is a men's chain bracelet valued differently from a women's?

No. Both are valued at the same per-gram rate. The gender categorisation is irrelevant to resale value.

Does the chain style (curb, rope, Cuban) affect value?

No. All chain styles are valued at the same per-gram rate. Link pattern is cosmetic.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What purity are men's chain bracelets?

Most are 22K. Some modern designs use 18K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a broken or kinked chain bracelet?

Yes. Physical damage does not affect gold purity.

How long to sell?

15–25 minutes.

What is a nethichutti?

A nethichutti is a traditional South Indian (Tamil) forehead ornament worn at the centre of the forehead by brides, suspended from the parting of the hair.

What is the difference between a nethichutti and a maang tikka?

Both are forehead ornaments. A nethichutti is the South Indian Tamil name; maang tikka is the North Indian Hindi name. They are the same type of ornament valued the same way at resale.

No. Stones and pearls are removed before weighing and returned. Only the gold portion is paid.

title: How to Check Gold Purity at Home: 5 Methods Explained
metaTitle: How to Check Gold Purity at Home | Gold Testing Guide India
description: Before selling gold, many people want to estimate their gold's purity at home before visiting a buyer. Several methods exist - from simple magnet tests to density calculations. Each…

source.title: How to Check Gold Purity at Home

keywords.keyword: how to check gold purity at home

html:
Before selling gold, many people want to estimate their gold's purity at home before visiting a buyer. Several methods exist - from simple magnet tests to density calculations. Each has different accuracy levels and limitations.

This guide covers all 5 home testing methods, what they can and cannot tell you, and why the XRF machine test at a reputable gold buyer remains the only definitive answer.

At a Glance

Most accurate home method

BIS hallmark check (999/916/750)

Most common mistake

Trusting acid test colour alone

Magnet test tells you

Whether it is NOT gold (not the karat)

Definitive professional test

XRF machine (±0.1% accurate)

Last Updated

May 2026

Method 1: Check the BIS Hallmark (Most Reliable Home Method)

Look for the BIS hallmark stamped on your jewellery. Since 2021, all gold sold in India must carry a 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID). The hallmark includes the purity code: 999 = 24K, 916 = 22K, 750 = 18K, 585 = 14K.

You can verify the HUID on the BIS Care mobile app (available on Android and iOS). This is the most reliable home check - though it applies only to hallmarked jewellery bought after 2021.

Method 2: Magnet Test

Hold a strong magnet near your gold. Pure gold is not magnetic - it will not be attracted to the magnet. If your jewellery is attracted to the magnet, it likely contains iron or steel and is not solid gold.

Important limitation: this test only tells you if something is definitely NOT gold. It cannot distinguish between 24K, 22K and 18K. Brass, copper and silver are also non-magnetic but are not gold.

Method 3: Float/Density Test

Gold is very dense (19.3 g/cm³). Drop your piece into a glass of water. Real gold should sink immediately. Fake gold (plated brass or hollow pieces) may float or sink slowly.

Limitation: most gold jewellery has some hollow sections or alloys that can affect the result. This test is a rough indicator, not a reliable purity test.

Method 4: Acid Test (Home Kit)

Gold acid test kits are available online (typically ₹200–500). You make a small scratch on a touchstone, rub the gold on it, and apply acid. The colour reaction indicates approximate karat range.

Accuracy: ±2–3K (approximate range, not exact). The acid test also scratches the touchstone and can slightly damage the piece surface. Home kits are less accurate than professional acid testing at a lab.

Method 5: Electronic Gold Tester

Handheld electronic gold testers (available online, ₹1,500–5,000) apply a small electrical signal to the piece and estimate purity based on conductivity. They are quick (10–20 seconds) but accuracy is limited - typically ±3–5K.

They can also give false readings on plated gold, heavily alloyed pieces and soldered sections.

Frequently Asked Questions

How can I check if my gold is 22K or 18K at home?

Does a magnet test tell me the karat of my gold?

No. The magnet test only tells you if something is NOT gold (if it attracts a magnet). It cannot distinguish between 24K, 22K and 18K.

Can I use the BIS Care app to check my gold?

Yes. If your gold has a 6-digit HUID hallmark, you can verify purity on the BIS Care app. This applies to hallmarked jewellery bought in India after 2021.

Is the acid test accurate?

The acid test gives an approximate range (±2–3K), not an exact reading. It is better than nothing but not reliable enough for resale pricing.

How accurate is a home electronic gold tester?

Typically ±3–5K accurate. Better than a magnet test but less reliable than XRF. Not recommended for resale price estimation.

A gold oval ring features an oval-shaped profile - either an oval band cross-section, an oval-top setting for a gemstone, or an oval motif. Oval rings are particularly popular for engagement and cocktail rings where a large oval stone (diamond, ruby, emerald) is set on an oval-shaped prong setting.

  • Large oval diamond/gemstone solitaire - stone removed at resale
  • Oval-shaped Indian traditional ring - same per-gram rate
  • Vintage oval cabochon ring - stone removed, gold base paid

Resale Value & Worked Example

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing
  • No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

How much is a gold oval ring worth today?

A 5g 22K oval ring is worth ₹69,845. A 10g piece brings ₹1,39,690.

Are oval stones paid at a gold buyer?

No. Oval diamonds or gemstones are removed and returned. Only the gold setting is paid.

Yes.

15–20 minutes.

Should I get a diamond certificate before selling?

Yes - if you want to maximise value of the oval diamond, a GIA/IGI certificate helps separate diamond valuation.

A veni is a traditional South Indian hair ornament — gold clips, chains or shaped pendants woven into the hair or braid.

title: Selling Inherited Gold in India: Complete Guide
metaTitle: Selling Inherited Gold | Legal Guide India 2026
description: Inherited gold — jewellery or coins received through a will or family succession — is one of the most common forms of gold that Indians sell. Many people are unsure of the legal…
html:
Inherited gold — jewellery or coins received through a will or family succession — is one of the most common forms of gold that Indians sell. Many people are unsure of the legal requirements: Can you sell without the original purchase bill? What KYC is needed? What are the tax implications?

This guide answers all those questions clearly.

At a Glance

Can you sell inherited gold?

Yes — fully legal

Original purchase bill required?

No — not needed for sale

KYC required

Aadhaar (all) + PAN (if >₹2L)

Tax on sale

LTCG 12.5% if held >24 months

Purity determined by

XRF machine test at branch

Last Updated

May 2026

Is It Legal to Sell Inherited Gold?

Yes. Selling inherited gold is completely legal in India. Gold received through inheritance, a will (vasiyat) or family succession is your property and can be sold freely.

There is no restriction on selling inherited jewellery. The only requirements are standard KYC documents — the same as for any gold sale.

Documents Required to Sell Inherited Gold

Document

Required?

Notes

Aadhaar Card

Yes — mandatory for all gold sales

Prevention of Money Laundering Act

PAN Card

Yes — if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000

Income Tax Act Section 114B

Original purchase bill

No — not required

XRF determines purity instead

Will / succession certificate

Not required for sale

May help for tax cost-basis

Death certificate of original owner

Not required for sale

Not asked by gold buyer

What Happens Without the Original Bill

The original purchase bill is not needed to sell at a gold buyer. XRF machine testing determines the exact purity of the inherited gold piece in 30–60 seconds. You are paid the IBJA rate × weight × purity fraction — regardless of when the original owner bought it or at what price.

However, without the original purchase bill, you may not be able to prove the cost of acquisition to the Income Tax Department for LTCG purposes.

Tax on Selling Inherited Gold

Inherited gold is subject to Capital Gains Tax when sold:

• Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG): If the original owner held the gold for more than 24 months before death AND you (as heir) have held it for any period after inheritance, the combined holding period applies. LTCG rate: 12.5% (without indexation, post Budget 2024).

• Short-Term Capital Gain: If total holding period is under 24 months, the gain is added to your income slab.

• Cost of acquisition: For inherited gold, the cost basis is the fair market value on the date of inheritance (not the original purchase price). If you have a valuation certificate from the date of inheritance, this helps.

Consult a tax advisor for your specific situation.

  • Bring the gold jewellery/coins and your Aadhaar card (+ PAN if expected sale >₹2L)
  • The branch team performs free XRF testing to determine exact purity
  • Gold is weighed on calibrated digital scales
  • You receive the IBJA rate × weight × purity fraction in cash or bank transfer
  • A signed receipt is issued to you — retain it for tax purposes

Special Situations

  • Multiple heirs: If the gold is shared among heirs, each person's share can be sold by them individually with their own KYC.
  • Gold received before hallmarking era: No hallmark is fine — XRF tests regardless.
  • Very old/antique inherited gold: Age and antique value add no premium at a gold buyer. Only the gold content is paid.
  • Selling on behalf of an elderly heir: The heir must be present with their own Aadhaar.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell inherited gold without the original bill?

Yes. No original purchase bill is needed. XRF testing determines purity and you are paid the IBJA rate by weight.

What documents do I need to sell inherited gold?

Aadhaar card (mandatory for all). PAN card (mandatory if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000).

Do I need to show the will or succession certificate?

No. Gold buyers do not ask for the will or succession documents. Only standard KYC (Aadhaar + PAN if >₹2L) is needed.

Is there tax on selling inherited gold?

Yes — Capital Gains Tax applies. If the combined holding period (original owner + heir) exceeds 24 months, LTCG at 12.5% applies on the gain. Consult a tax advisor.

What is the cost of acquisition for inherited gold for tax purposes?

For inherited gold, the cost basis is typically the fair market value on the date you inherited it, not the original purchase price. A valuation certificate from the inheritance date helps.

Can I sell gold I inherited 10 years ago?

Yes. There is no time limit on selling inherited gold.

What if multiple family members inherited the same gold?

Each heir sells their proportionate share with their own Aadhaar + PAN. If the gold is physically combined, it should be divided or one person designated to sell with others’ consent documented.

Most South Indian temple jewellery is 22K (916). Some older heirloom pieces may be 20K–21K. XRF at the branch confirms exact purity.

title: Difference Between 22K and 24K Gold: Complete Comparison
metaTitle: 22K vs 24K Gold | Difference Explained India 2026
description: 22K and 24K are the two most common gold purities discussed in India - 24K is pure gold, while 22K is gold alloyed with other metals for strength. Understanding the difference helps…
html:
22K and 24K are the two most common gold purities discussed in India - 24K is pure gold, while 22K is gold alloyed with other metals for strength. Understanding the difference helps you make informed decisions whether buying, gifting or selling gold.

This guide compares purity, durability, colour, pricing and which is better suited for jewellery versus investment.

At a Glance

24K gold purity

999 - 99.9% pure gold

22K gold purity

916 - 91.6% pure gold

24K rate today

₹15,250/g

22K rate today

₹13,965/g

Price difference (per gram)

₹1,285

Better for jewellery

22K (more durable)

Better for investment

24K (maximum purity)

Last Updated

May 2026

Purity: The Core Difference

24K gold is 99.9% pure - essentially as pure as gold can be refined. 22K gold is 91.6% pure, with the remaining 8.4% made up of alloying metals (typically copper, silver or zinc).

The BIS hallmark codes reflect this: 24K carries the 999 mark; 22K carries the 916 mark.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Factor

24K Gold

22K Gold

Purity

99.9% (999)

91.6% (916)

Colour

Deep rich yellow

Slightly less intense yellow

Durability

Soft, scratches easily

Harder, more durable

Best for

Coins, bars, investment

Jewellery (rings, necklaces, bangles)

Price per gram today

₹15,250

₹13,965

Can hold gemstones well?

No - too soft

Yes - standard for Indian jewellery

Resale value (per gram)

Higher

Lower (but still high purity)

Why Is 22K Used for Jewellery Instead of 24K?

Pure 24K gold is very soft - it bends and scratches easily, making it impractical for daily-wear jewellery like rings and bangles that endure friction and impact. Alloying gold with copper, silver or zinc (creating 22K) significantly increases hardness and durability while retaining a rich gold colour.

This is why most traditional Indian jewellery - necklaces, bangles, earrings - is crafted in 22K gold, while 24K is reserved for coins, bars and certain ceremonial pieces.

Which Is Better for Resale?

24K gold technically has a higher per-gram resale rate (₹15,250 vs ₹13,965) since it has zero alloy content. However, this does not mean 24K jewellery is 'better' - it simply reflects purity.

For a 10g piece: 24K = ₹1,52,500 vs 22K = ₹1,39,690. The ₹12,810 difference reflects the 8.4% non-gold content in 22K, not any quality judgment. Both are valued fairly at their true purity through XRF testing.

How to Tell Which Purity You Have

  • Check the BIS hallmark: look for 999 (24K) or 916 (22K) stamped on the piece
  • Visual colour alone is unreliable - always confirm with hallmark or XRF

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the price difference between 22K and 24K gold today?

24K is ₹15,250/g; 22K is ₹13,965/g - a difference of ₹1,285 per gram, reflecting 24K's higher purity.

Is 24K gold better than 22K gold?

Neither is "better" - they serve different purposes. 24K is purer and better for investment (coins, bars). 22K is more durable and better suited for daily-wear jewellery.

Can jewellery be made from 24K gold?

Rarely, because 24K is too soft for jewellery that needs durability. Some ceremonial or investment-grade pieces use 24K, but most jewellery is 22K or lower.

How much more do I get selling 24K gold vs 22K?

For the same weight, 24K pays the full ₹15,250/g rate, while 22K pays ₹13,965/g (91.6% of the 24K rate). A 10g piece: 24K = ₹1,52,500, 22K = ₹1,39,690.

Is 22K gold considered "real" gold?

Yes. 22K (91.6% pure) is genuine, high-purity gold - it is simply alloyed with other metals for strength. Most fine jewellery worldwide uses 18K–22K, not 24K.

html:
A promise ring symbolises a couple's commitment, often given before an engagement ring as a token of devotion. Promise rings are typically simpler and lighter than engagement rings, ranging from thin plain bands to designs with a small accent stone.

At resale, only gold weight and purity determine cash value. Any accent stone is removed and handled separately.

At a Glance

Stone-accented promise ring

3g – 8g gold

Last Updated

Common Types & Use Cases

  • Thin plain promise band - minimalist commitment symbol, 1.5g–4g
  • Standard promise ring - fashion/gift piece, 3g–7g
  • Stone-accented promise ring - small diamond/birthstone, stone removed at resale
  • Couple's matching promise rings - each weighed individually
  • Engraved promise ring - engraving adds no premium

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 4g 22K promise ring: 4 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹55,876.

For a stone-set 6g piece (1g stone): net gold 5g; payout = ₹69,845. The promise/commitment symbolism adds no resale premium.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing
  • Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing
  • No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement
  • Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold promise ring worth today?

A 4g 22K promise ring is worth ₹55,876. A 6g piece brings ₹83,814.

Is a promise ring valued differently from an engagement ring?

No. Both are valued at the same per-gram rate. Promise rings are typically lighter and simpler in design, which means a lower total weight and payout.

Are stones in a promise ring paid?

No. Stones removed and returned. Only gold portion paid.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Promise rings typically below ₹2L PAN threshold.

What purity?

Often 18K (delicate Western-style design) or 22K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a broken promise ring?

Yes.

How long?

10–15 minutes.

source.title: Gold Dog Tag Pendant - Resale Value

html:
A gold dog tag pendant is a flat, rectangular pendant inspired by military identification tags - a popular men's fashion accessory, often engraved with a name, date or message. Dog tag pendants are typically worn on a chain and range from thin lightweight designs to thick statement pieces.

At resale, only the gold weight and purity determine cash value. Engraving adds no premium.

At a Glance

Standard dog tag pendant

6g – 14g

Heavy thick dog tag

12g – 22g

Last Updated

Common Types & Use Cases

  • Thin gold dog tag - men's fashion piece, 4g–8g
  • Standard engraved dog tag - name/date inscription, 6g–14g
  • Heavy thick dog tag pendant - statement piece, 12g–22g
  • Dual dog tag set on a chain - each tag weighed together
  • Dog tag with attached chain - pendant and chain weighed together or separately

Resale Value & Worked Example

For an 8g 22K dog tag pendant: 8 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,11,752.

For a heavy 16g piece: ₹2,23,504. The engraving (name, date, message) adds no resale premium.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing
  • Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing
  • No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement
  • Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold dog tag pendant worth today?

An 8g 22K dog tag is worth ₹1,11,752. A 16g heavy piece brings ₹2,23,504.

Does the engraving on a dog tag add resale value?

No. Gold buyers pay only for gold weight and purity. Engraved text adds no resale premium.

Can I sell the dog tag without the chain?

Yes. Pendant and chain are weighed separately if sold individually.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Most dog tags well below ₹2L PAN threshold.

What purity are dog tag pendants?

Most are 22K or 18K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a scratched or worn dog tag?

Yes. Physical wear does not affect gold purity.

How long to sell?

10–15 minutes.

source.title: Gold Hallmark Verification Online - BIS Care App Guide

html:
Since 2021, BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) mandates that all gold jewellery sold in India carry a unique 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID). This allows any buyer or seller to verify the jewellery's hallmark certification online through the official BIS Care mobile app.

This guide walks through verifying your gold's hallmark step by step before selling.

At a Glance

Verification app

BIS Care (official, free)

Available on

Android and iOS

HUID format

6-digit alphanumeric code

What it confirms

Purity, jeweller, hallmarking centre, date

Cost to verify

Free

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is HUID Hallmark Verification?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a 6-digit alphanumeric code engraved on BIS-hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India since June 2021. Each HUID is unique to that specific piece and is recorded in the BIS database along with details like purity, the assaying & hallmarking centre, and the jeweller.

Verifying the HUID confirms the piece is genuinely BIS-certified at the stated purity - useful both when buying and before selling.

Step-by-Step: How to Verify Your Gold’s Hallmark

  • Download the official "BIS Care" app from Google Play Store or Apple App Store
  • Open the app and select "Verify HUID" or similar option from the menu
  • Locate the 6-digit HUID code engraved on your jewellery (usually near other hallmark symbols)
  • Enter the HUID code into the app
  • The app displays verification details: purity, hallmarking centre, and registration status
  • Cross-check the displayed purity matches what you expect (916 for 22K, etc.)

What the BIS Care App Shows You

Information Displayed

What It Means

Purity (Fineness)

Confirms 999/916/750/585 grading

Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC)

Where the piece was tested and certified

Registration Status

Confirms the HUID is genuine and registered

Jeweller Details

Registered jeweller who sold the piece (where available)

What If My Gold Has No HUID?

Does Hallmark Verification Affect Resale Price?

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I verify my gold’s hallmark online?

Download the official BIS Care app (Android/iOS), enter your jewellery’s 6-digit HUID code, and the app displays purity and certification details.

What is a HUID number?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a unique 6-digit alphanumeric code assigned to each piece of BIS-hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India since June 2021.

Where do I find the HUID code on my jewellery?

It is engraved near other hallmark symbols, typically on the inside of rings/bangles or on a small tag/clasp for chains and necklaces.

What if my gold jewellery has no HUID?

This is normal for jewellery purchased before June 2021. It does not indicate lower quality - XRF testing at a gold buyer determines exact purity regardless.

Is the BIS Care app free?

Yes. It is the official free app from the Bureau of Indian Standards, available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

Can a hallmark be faked?

Counterfeit hallmarks exist, which is why XRF verification at the time of resale is important - it independently confirms actual purity rather than relying solely on stamped marks.

html:
Kundan jewellery is a traditional Indian jewellery technique originating from Rajasthan, featuring uncut glass stones (kund) set in gold using a refined gold foil (kundankari) technique. Unlike polki (which uses real uncut diamonds), kundan uses high-quality glass to replicate the look of precious stones.

At resale, only the gold content is paid. Kundan glass stones have no resale value at a gold buyer and are excluded from the weight.

Common Types & Use Cases

  • Kundan earrings - glass-set earrings, 5g–18g of gold
  • Kundan necklace - elaborate glass-set necklace, 15g–40g of gold
  • Kundan maang tikka - forehead ornament with kundan, 4g–12g of gold
  • Full kundan bridal set (necklace + earrings + tikka + bangles) - 40g–100g+ of gold
  • Heirloom kundan jewellery - same per-gram rate regardless of age or craftsmanship

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 25g kundan necklace (gold weight only, kundan glass excluded): 25 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹3,49,225.

For a full bridal kundan set at 70g of gold: ₹9,77,830.

Key distinction: kundan uses glass (no resale value). Polki uses real uncut diamonds (which need separate diamond specialist valuation). Confirm with XRF and visual inspection at the branch.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing
  • Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing
  • No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement
  • Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is gold kundan jewellery worth today?

Only the gold portion is paid. A 25g kundan necklace (gold only) is worth ₹3,49,225.

What is kundan jewellery?

Kundan is a traditional Rajasthani jewellery technique using uncut glass stones set in gold using a refined gold foil. The result resembles precious-stone jewellery but uses glass.

What is the difference between kundan and polki?

Kundan uses glass stones; polki uses real uncut natural diamonds. At a gold buyer, neither the kundan glass nor the polki diamonds add to the gold payout - but polki stones can be separately assessed by a diamond specialist.

Are the kundan glass stones paid at resale?

No. Kundan glass has no resale value. Only the gold setting and base are paid.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 - most kundan sets exceed this.

What purity is kundan jewellery gold?

Traditional kundan uses 22K or 24K gold foil (kundankari). Most pieces are 22K. XRF confirms.

How many grams is 10 pavans?

How many sovereigns is 10 pavans?

What Jewellery Weighs Around 40 Grams

  • Exactly 5 pavans = 40g of gold
  • Common South Indian weight unit: 5 sovereigns
  • 5 gold coins (each 8 grams)

Resale Formula

Tax Treatment

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG. Aadhaar mandatory; PAN if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Rate on wrong karat without disclosure
  • No written receipt

Frequently Asked Questions

What is 5 pavan gold price today?

5 pavans = 40g. At 22K: ₹5,58,760. At 24K: ₹6,10,000.

How many grams is 5 pavans?

1 pavan = 8 grams. So 5 pavans = 5 × 8 = 40 grams.

How many sovereigns is 5 pavans?

Pavan and sovereign are the same unit. 5 pavans = 5 sovereigns = 40 grams.

What documents are needed to sell gold pavans?

Aadhaar is mandatory. PAN is required if the total sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 - ₹5,58,760 exceeds this threshold.

Is pavan the same as savaran?

1 pavan = 1 savaran = 1 sovereign = 8 grams. All three names refer to the same unit used in South India.

Does the age or condition of the gold affect pavan pricing?

No. Only the gold purity (tested by XRF) and weight (in grams) determine the price. Age, scratches and tarnish do not matter.

html:
Filigree jewellery (called tarkashi in Hindi, or koftgari in some regions) is a delicate jewellery technique where thin gold wire is twisted and curled into intricate lacy patterns. Famous filigree-making centres in India include Karimnagar (Telangana), Cuttack (Odisha) and parts of Rajasthan.

At resale, filigree craftsmanship adds no premium. Only the gold weight and purity determine cash value. Because filigree uses very fine wire, pieces are typically lighter than solid gold jewellery of the same visual size.

Common Types & Use Cases

  • Karimnagar filigree earrings — 2g–8g, intricate wire lace design
  • Cuttack filigree pendant — 3g–10g, famous Odisha style
  • Filigree necklace (collar style) — 8g–25g
  • Rajasthani filigree bracelet — 6g–18g
  • Heirloom filigree jewellery — heritage craftsmanship adds no resale premium

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 10g 22K filigree necklace: 10 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,39,690.

For a 20g piece: ₹2,79,380. Important note: filigree uses very fine gold wire, which is accurately weighed on precision scales. The intricate craftsmanship is paid at the same per-gram rate as plain gold — not more, not less.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

  • Stones or lac weighed with gold — insist on removal before weighing
  • Visual purity check instead of XRF — always request machine testing
  • No written receipt — a signed receipt is a legal requirement
  • Making charge deductions at resale — these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is gold filigree jewellery worth today?

A 10g 22K filigree piece is worth ₹1,39,690. A 20g piece brings ₹2,79,380.

Does the intricate filigree craftsmanship add resale value?

No. Gold buyers pay only for the weight of gold wire and the purity. Filigree, tarkashi and koftgari craftsmanship add no premium at resale, regardless of their artistic value.

Is filigree jewellery lighter than solid gold?

Yes. Filigree uses thin twisted wire, so pieces look larger than their weight suggests. A 10g filigree necklace may appear as large as a 20g solid necklace.

Are stones embedded in filigree paid?

No. Stones are removed before weighing and returned to you.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Most filigree pieces are below ₹2L PAN threshold.

What purity is filigree gold?

Most is 22K. Karimnagar filigree is typically 22K. XRF at the branch confirms.

How is very fine filigree wire weighed accurately?

On precision digital scales accurate to 0.01g. Even light filigree pieces are weighed precisely.

source.title: Best Time to Sell Gold in India

html:
People often wonder whether to wait for a higher gold price before selling. While timing the gold market is genuinely difficult, there are predictable seasonal and cyclical patterns that can help sellers make more informed decisions.

This guide covers what drives gold prices in India, seasonal patterns and a practical rule of thumb for when to sell.

At a Glance

Gold price driver (global)

US dollar / international commodity markets

Gold price driver (India)

IBJA daily rate, USD-INR exchange rate

Seasonal high

Oct–Dec (wedding + Diwali/Dhanteras season)

Seasonal low

May–July (summer, lower jewellery buying)

Rate changes

Daily (IBJA publishes every trading day)

Best personal timing

When you need the cash — not when you predict the peak

Last Updated

May 2026

What Drives Gold Prices in India?

Gold prices in India are determined primarily by the international commodity price (USD per troy ounce) converted at the daily USD-INR exchange rate. The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the benchmark rate each trading day.

This means gold price changes in India are mostly driven by global factors: US Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, geopolitical events, global inflation and dollar strength/weakness. Indian seasonal demand (festivals, weddings) has a smaller but observable impact.

Seasonal Patterns in Indian Gold Prices

Period

Typical Demand Trend

Price Implication

Oct–Dec (Navratri, Diwali, Dhanteras, wedding season)

High buying demand

Prices may be elevated

Jan–Mar (Pongal, Makar Sankranti, Valentines)

Moderate buying demand

Apr–Jun (Akshaya Tritiya peak in Apr/May)

Akshaya Tritiya buying spike

Brief price uptick possible

Jul–Sep (Monsoon, Shraadh period)

Lowest jewellery buying

Prices may dip slightly

The Honest Answer: Timing Is Very Difficult

Gold price prediction is notoriously difficult — even professional analysts regularly get it wrong. The factors driving price (geopolitics, Fed decisions, currency movements) are genuinely unpredictable.

The practical guidance most financial advisors give: if you have a reason to sell (need cash, want to reinvest, upgrading jewellery), sell when the rate is reasonable — don't wait for a peak that may or may not come.

What You Can Control: Getting the Best Rate Today

  • Check the live IBJA rate before visiting any buyer — this is your benchmark
  • Visit during market hours (Mon–Fri, before 4 PM) when IBJA rate is confirmed for the day
  • Compare offers from multiple buyers if selling a large quantity
  • Sell all pieces at once rather than multiple small visits (no rate advantage to splitting, but saves time)
  • Avoid selling during economic disturbances when buyers may widen their spread

Does Selling During Festivals Give a Better Price?

Not usually. While gold buying demand peaks during Dhanteras and Akshaya Tritiya, gold buyers pay IBJA rates — they do not pay a 'festival premium' above the benchmark. The IBJA rate itself may be slightly higher during demand peaks, but the direct impact on your resale rate is marginal and unpredictable.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the best time to sell gold in India?

There is no reliably predictable "best time." Gold prices move on global factors. Practically: sell when the IBJA rate is strong relative to recent months and you have a need to sell.

Is Dhanteras a good time to sell gold?

Demand during Dhanteras is high, which may support prices. However, gold buyers pay IBJA rates regardless of the festival. The IBJA rate itself may be marginally higher, but this is not guaranteed.

Does the gold rate change daily?

Yes. The IBJA publishes a new rate every trading day (Monday–Friday). Rates can move significantly based on overnight global market movements.

Should I wait for gold price to go up before selling?

Only if you can afford to wait and have no urgent need. Market timing is difficult; many sellers who waited for a higher price saw prices fall instead. Sell when the rate is acceptable and you have a reason to sell.

Is Akshaya Tritiya a good time to sell gold?

Akshaya Tritiya is traditionally auspicious for buying gold, which supports demand and may slightly elevate prices. However, buyers pay IBJA rates and the practical impact on your resale price is small.

source.title: Selling Gold Online in India - Is It Safe?

html:
Several platforms offer to buy gold online in India — you send your jewellery by courier and receive payment digitally. While convenient, online gold selling carries significant risks compared to selling at a reputable physical buyer.

This guide explains how online gold selling works, what the risks are and how it compares to visiting a branch.

At a Glance

Online gold buying — legitimate?

Some platforms are legitimate; many are not

Main risk

Gold in transit, value disputes, delayed payment

Physical buyer advantage

Instant rate, immediate payment, XRF on the spot

Regulated by

No specific regulator for gold buying in India

Last Updated

May 2026

How Online Gold Selling Works

Online gold buyers typically follow this process: you request a quote online, they send you a courier kit, you pack and ship your gold, they receive and test it, then offer a price. If you accept, they transfer payment to your bank account.

The quote given online is usually preliminary — the actual offer may differ after they test the purity and weight at their facility.

Key Risks of Selling Gold Online

  • Gold in transit risk — if the courier is lost or damaged, the insurance claim process is complex and may not cover full market value
  • Price dispute after receipt — online buyers may claim lower purity or weight than expected, and you cannot be present during testing
  • Delayed payment — some platforms take several days or weeks to process and pay
  • Difficulty returning gold — if you reject their offer, getting gold returned can be slow and costly
  • Unregulated space — no specific regulator governs gold buying in India; consumer protection is limited
  • Scam platforms — some fraudulent platforms collect gold and disappear; verifying legitimacy is difficult

Online vs Physical Gold Buyer — Comparison

Convenience

High — from home

Moderate — branch visit needed

Speed of payment

2–7 days typically

Same day — immediate

Purity testing

Done at their facility (not visible to you)

XRF at branch in front of you

Price dispute risk

High — you cannot witness testing

Low — you see the results live

Gold-in-transit risk

Yes — courier risk

None

Receipt issued

Digital (may not be reliable)

Signed physical receipt guaranteed

Rate offered

Often below IBJA (spread wider)

IBJA-based rate

How to Verify an Online Gold Buyer (If You Choose to Use One)

  • Check company registration on MCA21 portal (Ministry of Corporate Affairs)
  • Verify GST registration (legitimate businesses have GST numbers)
  • Look for physical address and phone number — test by calling
  • Read independent reviews (not testimonials on their own site)
  • Check insurance coverage explicitly — get it in writing before shipping
  • Start with a small piece to test the process before sending large quantities

Why a Physical Buyer Is Safer

Frequently Asked Questions

Is selling gold online in India safe?

Some platforms are legitimate, but the process carries significant risks: gold in transit, price disputes you cannot witness, and delayed payment. Physical buyers are safer and faster.

Which is better — selling gold online or at a branch?

Do online gold buyers offer better rates?

Generally no. Online buyers have higher operational costs (courier, logistics) and often offer below-IBJA rates. Physical buyers with low overhead can offer competitive IBJA-based rates.

What if I cannot travel to a branch?

Is there any government regulation of online gold buyers?

No specific regulator governs gold buying in India. This makes the online space riskier than regulated financial products.

What documents do I need to sell gold online?

Requirements vary by platform, but generally Aadhaar and PAN are needed. Physical buyers require the same KYC.

Can I be scammed when selling gold online?

Yes. Fraudulent platforms exist. Always verify company registration and physical address before shipping your gold to any online buyer.

html:
Getting the best price for your gold isn't about negotiating — it's about knowing what you should receive and ensuring nothing is unfairly deducted. Gold is a commodity valued at the daily IBJA rate; the price is transparent and calculable. What varies between buyers is how honestly they apply that rate.

These 7 tips help you walk into any gold buying transaction fully prepared.

At a Glance

Key number to know

Today's IBJA 22K rate per gram

Key formula

Weight × Purity Fraction × 24K Rate

Non-negotiable deductions

Stones, lac, non-gold elements only

Illegal deductions

Making charges, handling fees, arbitrary cuts

Best protection

Know the rate before you walk in

Last Updated

May 2026

Tip 1: Know the Live IBJA Rate Before You Go

The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the gold rate each trading day. Check it before visiting any buyer. This is your benchmark — the maximum you can receive per gram for each purity level.

22K rate today: ₹13,965/g. 24K rate today: ₹15,250/g.

Tip 2: Calculate Your Expected Payout Before Visiting

Tip 3: Insist on XRF Testing (Not Just Visual/Acid)

  • XRF (X-ray fluorescence) is the most accurate purity test — accurate to ±0.1%
  • Acid tests and visual estimates are less accurate and can understate purity
  • If a buyer refuses XRF or charges for testing, that is a red flag

Tip 4: Know What CAN and CANNOT Be Deducted

Tip 5: Get a Written Receipt

A signed receipt is a legal requirement in India for gold transactions. It should state: weight, purity, rate per gram, total amount paid and your KYC details. Refuse to sell to any buyer who will not issue a receipt.

Tip 6: Bring Your KYC Ready

Aadhaar is mandatory for all gold sales. PAN is required if your total sale exceeds ₹2,00,000. Having these ready speeds up the process and avoids any delay at the branch.

Tip 7: Choose a Regulated, Reputable Buyer

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I get the best price for my gold?

Check the live IBJA rate first, calculate your expected payout, insist on XRF testing, and choose a reputable buyer who does not make arbitrary deductions.

Are making charges deducted when selling gold?

No. Making charges are paid when buying new jewellery and are not recoverable at resale. No legitimate gold buyer deducts making charges.

What is the IBJA rate?

IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the daily benchmark gold price. Today's 22K rate is ₹13,965/g.

Should I get multiple quotes before selling?

Yes, especially for large quantities. The IBJA rate is the benchmark; compare how closely different buyers offer this rate.

Can I negotiate the gold buying rate?

The per-gram rate is based on IBJA — there is little room to negotiate the rate itself. The protection is ensuring no unfair deductions and using XRF testing.

Aadhaar card (mandatory). PAN card (if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000).

·         Stones or lac weighed with gold — insist on removal before weighing

·         Visual purity check instead of XRF — always request machine testing

·         Making charge deductions at resale — these do not apply

What purity?

Most are 18K or 22K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell the drops separately?

Yes. Each section can be weighed separately.

How long?

15–25 minutes.

No. Stones removed and returned.

A gold rope bracelet features the same twisted-spiral link design as a rope chain, but worn on the wrist. Rope bracelets are popular for men's jewellery and as bold fashion bracelets. They are typically heavier than other bracelet styles due to the dense rope construction.

At resale, only gold weight and purity determine cash value - the rope-twist pattern adds no premium.
