·         Standard rope bracelet - bold daily wear, 15g–30g

·         Heavy rope bracelet - statement piece, 25g–50g

·         Men's gold rope bracelet - same per-gram rate as women's

·         Rope bracelet with clasp/charm - charm weighed with bracelet

Resale Value & Worked Example

For an 18g 22K rope bracelet: 18 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,51,442.

For a 30g piece: ₹4,19,070. All rope bracelet sales at today's rate exceed ₹2,00,000 - PAN required.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·         Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·         Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·         No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·         Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold rope bracelet worth today?

An 18g 22K rope bracelet is worth ₹2,51,442. A 30g piece brings ₹4,19,070.

Is a rope bracelet the same as a rope chain on the wrist?

Yes. The construction is identical - twisted spiral links. Worn on wrist = rope bracelet; worn around neck = rope chain. Same per-gram rate.

Do I need PAN?

Yes - virtually all rope bracelets exceed ₹2,00,000 at today's rates.

What purity?

Most are 22K or 18K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a broken rope bracelet?

Yes. Physical damage does not affect gold purity.

How long?

20–30 minutes.

Is the rope pattern more valuable than other bracelet styles?

No. All styles valued at the same per-gram rate.

html:
The tree of life is a universal symbol representing growth, family, connection and eternity, found across multiple cultures and religions. Gold tree of life pendants are popular gift items and fashion pieces, ranging from minimalist wire designs to elaborate filigree-style pieces.

At resale, only the gold weight and purity determine cash value. The symbolic meaning and artistic design add no resale premium.

At a Glance

Common Types & Use Cases

·         Small minimalist gold tree pendant - 2g–5g

·         Standard tree of life pendant - gift/fashion, 4g–9g

·         Large ornate tree with filigree branches - 7g–14g

·         Tree of life with birthstone leaves - stones removed at resale

·         Family tree pendant (personalised) - same per-gram rate

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 5g plain 22K tree of life: 5 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹69,845.

For a 10g ornate piece: ₹1,39,690. The symbolic and artistic design adds no resale premium.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·         Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·         Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·         No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·         Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold tree of life pendant worth today?

A 5g 22K piece is worth ₹69,845. A 10g ornate pendant brings ₹1,39,690.

Does the tree of life symbol add resale value?

No. Gold buyers pay for gold weight and purity only.

Are birthstones or gems in the pendant paid?

No. Stones removed and returned.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Tree of life pendants typically below ₹2L.

What purity?

Most are 18K or 22K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a bent tree of life pendant?

Yes. Physical damage does not affect purity.

How long?

10–15 minutes.

title: Gold Hallmark Types in India: BIS, HUID, KDM & Older Marks Explained
metaTitle: Gold Hallmark Types | BIS HUID KDM Explained India
description: A gold hallmark is an official mark stamped on gold jewellery confirming its purity has been tested and certified. In India, hallmarks are governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards…
html:
A gold hallmark is an official mark stamped on gold jewellery confirming its purity has been tested and certified. In India, hallmarks are governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Understanding the different hallmark types helps you know what you have before selling.

This guide covers every hallmark type found on Indian gold jewellery and what each means for resale.

At a Glance

Current standard (2021–)

BIS 6-symbol mark with HUID

Old BIS mark (pre-2021)

BIS mark without HUID

KDM mark

Old mark for 916 solder-joined jewellery

Fineness code

999/916/750/585 - purity in parts per thousand

How to verify

BIS Care app (free, Android/iOS)

Last Updated

May 2026

The 6 Official BIS Hallmark Symbols (Current Standard)

Symbol

What It Means

BIS Logo (triangle with letters)

Confirms BIS certification

Fineness/Purity Mark

999=24K, 916=22K, 750=18K, 585=14K, 375=9K

Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC) ID

Code of the testing lab

Jeweller's ID Mark

Registered jeweller who made/sold the piece

Year of Hallmarking (letter code)

Year the piece was certified

HUID (6-digit alphanumeric)

Unique ID for that specific piece (post-June 2021)

What Is a HUID?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a 6-digit alphanumeric code mandated since June 2021. Each piece of gold jewellery sold in India must now have a unique HUID registered in the BIS database. You can verify any HUID using the free BIS Care mobile app.

What Is the KDM Hallmark?

KDM stands for cadmium - an older soldering material used in Indian goldsmithing. A KDM hallmark on jewellery indicates it was made using a cadmium-based solder, typically in the 22K (916) class. KDM marking is now banned in India (cadmium is toxic), but older jewellery with KDM marks still exists and can be sold freely at the standard gold rate.

Older BIS Hallmarks (Pre-2021, Without HUID)

What If My Gold Has No Hallmark?

Does Hallmark Type Affect Resale Price?

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the different types of gold hallmarks in India?

Current: 6-symbol BIS mark with HUID. Old: BIS mark without HUID. KDM: older cadmium-solder mark. Older pieces: international fineness marks only.

What does 916 mean on gold?

916 is the BIS fineness code for 22-karat gold - it contains 916 parts gold per 1,000 (91.6% pure gold).

What is the difference between a BIS hallmark and a HUID?

BIS hallmark is the full certification system. HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is the 6-digit code added since June 2021 to make each piece uniquely traceable.

Is KDM gold safe to sell?

Yes. KDM-marked gold is accepted by all reputable gold buyers. The KDM mark indicates an older soldering method, not a purity issue.

Does my gold need a hallmark to be sold?

How do I verify a HUID hallmark?

Use the free BIS Care app (Android/iOS). Enter the 6-digit HUID code to verify purity and certification details.

Does having a HUID get me a better price?

No. The price is based on XRF-tested purity, not the hallmark type.

Only the gold setting is paid. A 4g 22K setting is worth ₹55,876; at 18K: ₹45,750. The diamond requires separate valuation.

Does the diamond value show in the gold buyer price?

No. A gold buyer pays only for gold weight. Diamonds must be separately assessed by a certified diamond specialist.

Why is most diamond pendant gold 18K?

18K is harder and more durable for prong settings that hold diamonds. Most fine diamond jewellery globally uses 18K white or yellow gold.

Not required for the gold portion. For accurate diamond valuation, a certificate is very helpful.

Can I sell just the gold setting and keep the diamond?

Yes. Diamond removed and returned; you receive the gold weight × purity rate.

How long to sell?

20–30 minutes including diamond removal.

What Drives Gold Prices in India?

·         International gold price (USD/troy oz) - the primary driver

·         USD-INR exchange rate - a weaker rupee pushes Indian gold prices higher

·         US Federal Reserve interest rates - lower rates support gold

·         Geopolitical events - wars, crises, uncertainty boost gold demand

·         Indian seasonal demand (Diwali, Dhanteras, wedding season) - minor upward influence

·         RBI and government import duties - affect domestic prices independently of global prices

What Gold Rate History Tells Sellers

The long-term trend is clearly upward - gold in India has roughly doubled every 5–7 years over the past two decades. This means waiting often rewards patience, but the timing of peaks is genuinely unpredictable.

The 2020 COVID spike showed how quickly gold can surge 40%+ in months, then correct. Sellers who needed funds and sold in 2019 at ₹3,400/g still received fair value for their era; those who waited and sold in 2026 at ₹13,965/g received significantly more.

Practical guidance: if you need cash and the current rate is strong relative to recent years, selling now is rational. Waiting for a further peak carries the risk of a correction.

What was gold price in India 5 years ago?

In 2021, 22K gold was approximately ₹4,500–₹5,200/g. Today (May 2026) it is ₹13,965/g - a significant increase.

Has gold price always gone up in India?

Not in every year, but the 10–20 year trend is strongly upward. There have been correction periods (2012–2015, post-2020) but the long-term direction is up.

What was the highest gold price in India ever?

As of May 2026, current levels are at or near all-time highs for 22K gold in India.

Does the gold rate change every day in India?

Yes. The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the benchmark rate every trading day, based on international gold prices and the USD-INR rate.

Will gold rate go up or down in the future?

This cannot be predicted reliably. Gold is driven by global factors (USD, geopolitics, central bank policy) that are genuinely uncertain.

When was gold cheapest in the last 10 years?

Approximately 2014–2016, when 22K gold was around ₹2,400–₹2,700/g.

Is it better to sell gold now or wait?

If the rate is at a historically strong level and you have a need to sell, selling now is rational. Market timing is very difficult even for professionals.

html:
18K and 22K gold are the two most common gold purities in Indian jewellery. 22K dominates traditional Indian jewellery (necklaces, bangles, chains), while 18K is standard for diamond and gemstone jewellery. Understanding the difference helps you know what you have and what to expect when selling.

Note: we published a 22K vs 24K comparison separately. This page focuses specifically on the 18K vs 22K comparison.

Why 18K Is Used for Diamond Jewellery

18K gold is harder and more durable than 22K because it has more alloy content (25% copper/silver/zinc vs 8.4% in 22K). This extra hardness is important for prong settings that hold diamonds and gemstones in place - a 22K prong would be too soft and could bend, releasing the stone.

This is why engagement rings, diamond pendants, and most stone-set jewellery globally uses 18K (or 14K) gold rather than 22K.

Why 22K Is Used for Traditional Indian Jewellery

Traditional Indian jewellery (necklaces, bangles, haram) prioritises gold content and colour over extreme durability. 22K's higher purity gives a richer, warmer yellow colour and is seen as more prestigious for gifting and dowry.

Most Indian jewellery sold by traditional jewellers (from Tanishq to local goldsmiths) is 22K hallmarked.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between 18K and 22K gold?

22K has 91.6% gold (harder yellow, softer metal, used in traditional Indian jewellery). 18K has 75% gold (slightly paler, harder metal, used for diamond/stone-set jewellery).

Which is more expensive, 18K or 22K gold?

22K is more expensive per gram: ₹13,965/g vs 18K at ₹11,438/g - a difference of ₹2,527 per gram.

Is 22K better than 18K for resale?

22K gives a higher per-gram payout because it has more gold content. But the total value depends on the weight of each piece, not just the karat.

Which gold should I sell first - 18K or 22K?

There is no rule. Both can be sold whenever needed. 22K gives a higher rate per gram; 18K gives less per gram but is still fully valued at its correct purity rate.

How do I know if my ring is 18K or 22K?

Do most Indian necklaces come in 18K or 22K?

Most traditional Indian necklaces are 22K. Modern necklaces designed to hold diamonds may be 18K.

In India, the hamsa is also known as the 'Khamsa' and is worn as a protective talisman.

description: A gold solitaire pendant features a single diamond (or gemstone) set in a gold setting - the pendant version of the solitaire ring. Solitaire pendants are popular engagement and…
html:
A gold solitaire pendant features a single diamond (or gemstone) set in a gold setting - the pendant version of the solitaire ring. Solitaire pendants are popular engagement and anniversary gifts. At resale, the gold setting and the solitaire diamond are valued separately.

At a Glance

Gold setting (solitaire pendant)

2g – 6g gold

Solitaire diamond

Valued separately

18K gold setting (4g) today

₹45,750

22K gold setting (4g) today

₹55,876

Diamond

GIA/IGI certificate helps valuation

Last Updated

May 2026

Live Rate Today

At today's IBJA rate of ₹15,250 per gram for 24K, a 22K piece yields ₹13,965 per gram.

Designs & Weight Comparison

Component

Typical Weight

Value Basis

Notes

Small gold setting

2g – 4g

₹41,907 (3g avg)

Paid by gold weight

Standard gold setting

3g – 6g

₹62,860 (4.5g avg)

Paid by gold weight

Solitaire diamond

varies by carat

Separate valuation

GIA/IGI cert. advised

Common Types & Use Cases

·         Small solitaire pendant (0.25–0.5ct diamond) - 2g–4g gold setting

·         Standard solitaire pendant (0.5–1ct) - 3g–6g gold

·         Large solitaire pendant (1ct+) - 4g–8g gold setting

·         Vintage/heirloom solitaire pendant - same gold-only rate

·         Solitaire pendant on chain - setting and chain weighed separately

Resale Value & Worked Example

For a 4g 18K gold setting: 4 × 0.75 × ₹15,250 = ₹45,750. At 22K: ₹55,876.

The solitaire diamond is removed and returned. Diamond value depends on cut, colour, clarity and carat weight. A GIA or IGI certificate significantly assists diamond valuation.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

·         Stones or lac weighed with gold - insist on removal before weighing

·         Visual purity check instead of XRF - always request machine testing

·         No written receipt - a signed receipt is a legal requirement

·         Making charge deductions at resale - these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a gold solitaire pendant worth at a gold buyer?

The gold setting only: a 4g 18K setting is worth ₹45,750; at 22K: ₹55,876. The diamond requires separate gemological valuation.

Are solitaire pendant diamonds paid at a gold buyer?

No. A gold buyer pays for the gold weight only. The diamond is removed and returned.

Is most solitaire pendant gold 18K or 22K?

Most fine solitaire pendants use 18K gold (for durability of prong settings).

How is the solitaire diamond removed?

At the branch, carefully removed from the prong setting and returned to you.

Do I need a diamond certificate?

Not for the gold portion. For accurate diamond valuation, a GIA or IGI certificate is strongly advised.

Can I keep the diamond and sell just the gold?

Yes. Diamond returned; you receive the gold weight × purity rate.

How long to sell?

20–25 minutes including diamond removal.

Why Are There Different Gold Weight Units?

Different units emerged from different trading traditions. The gram became the international standard. Pavan (8g) is the South Indian conventional unit - widely used in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh for pricing jewellery. Tola (11.6638g) is the traditional North Indian and Pakistani unit still used in the Gulf gold market.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many grams in 1 pavan of gold?

1 pavan = 1 sovereign = 1 savaran = 8 grams.

How many grams in 1 tola of gold?

1 tola = 11.6638 grams exactly.

How do I convert tola to grams?

Multiply tolas by 11.6638. Example: 5 tolas = 5 × 11.6638 = 58.319 grams.

How do I convert pavans to grams?

Multiply pavans by 8. Example: 10 pavans = 10 × 8 = 80 grams.

What is the 22K gold rate per pavan today?

1 pavan = 8g. At today's 22K rate of ₹13,965/g: ₹1,11,752 per pavan.

What is the 22K gold rate per tola today?

1 tola = 11.6638g. At today's 22K rate: ₹1,62,932 per tola.

Why Gold Gives More Cash Per Piece

Gold is approximately 140× more valuable per gram than silver at current market rates. A 10g gold bangle at 22K is worth ₹1,39,690. A 10g silver bangle is worth approximately ₹900–₹1,000. The difference is stark.

For most Indian households, gold jewellery represents far more wealth than silver jewellery of similar weight, so there is rarely a meaningful 'choice' - the gold gives significantly more cash.

Where to Sell Silver in India

When Would You Sell Silver Instead of Gold?

·         You have silver but no gold

·         Your gold is earmarked for a specific purpose (dowry, gifting) but you need cash now

·         The silver piece has no sentimental value and the gold does

·         You need a small amount of cash and don't want to sell a full gold piece

Frequently Asked Questions

Which gives more cash - gold or silver?

Gold gives far more cash per gram. At today's rates, 1g of 22K gold is worth ₹13,965 while 1g of silver is worth approximately ₹90–₹100.

Is silver a better investment than gold?

Different risk/return profiles. Silver is more volatile and harder to sell. Gold is more liquid and has a more developed buyer ecosystem in India.

Can I sell my silver jewellery for cash easily in India?

Silver buyers exist but are less widespread than gold buyers. Specialist jewellery market dealers and online platforms are the main options.

Is the PAN threshold the same for silver as for gold?

Yes. PAN is required if a single transaction exceeds ₹2,00,000, regardless of whether you are selling gold or silver.

What is the silver rate today in India?

Silver rates change daily based on international commodity prices. As of May 2026, silver is approximately ₹90–₹100/g. Check a commodity rate website for the current rate.

Should I sell my silver to buy gold?

This is a personal financial decision. Gold has historically provided better long-term value in India, but silver has some uses where gold does not. Consult a financial advisor for investment decisions.

html:
Rose gold has grown significantly in popularity in India over the last decade - particularly for engagement rings, men's bands and contemporary jewellery. Its warm pink colour comes from mixing gold with copper, and it gives modern jewellery a distinctive look that yellow gold cannot replicate.

But what is rose gold worth when you want to sell it? Many sellers are surprised to learn that rose gold sells at exactly the same rate as yellow gold of the same purity - because the colour is irrelevant at resale. Only the gold content matters.

What Is Rose Gold Made Of?

Rose gold is an alloy - a mixture of pure gold with other metals. The exact recipe determines the depth of the pink colour:

• 18K rose gold (most common): 75% gold + ~22% copper + ~3% silver → warm pink
• 14K rose gold: 58.5% gold + higher copper → deeper, redder pink
• 9K rose gold: 37.5% gold + very high copper → reddish tone

The copper is what gives rose gold its colour. It is not a coating or plating - it is a through-and-through alloy. This means the colour will not wear off, unlike rhodium plating on white gold.

Will I Get Less for Rose Gold Because of the Copper?

No. You are paid for the gold content only - which is 75% of the weight for 18K. The copper (and trace silver) are separated during refining and not your concern as the seller.

The same as a 12g white or yellow gold ring of the same purity.

Per gram, 18K rose gold and 18K yellow gold are worth exactly the same. Only karat (purity) and weight determine resale value, not colour.

18K rose gold is worth ₹11,438/g today. A 10g rose gold piece is worth ₹1,14,375.

If you find the number 375 stamped on a piece of jewellery, you have 9 karat gold - the most common gold purity used in the UK, Australia and parts of Europe. It is not widely sold in Indian jewellery shops, but it frequently arrives in India as gifts from abroad or as pieces bought during international travel.

9K gold is genuine gold, but it contains only 37.5% pure gold. Understanding what it is worth - and that you can absolutely sell it in India - is what this guide covers.

What Is 9K Gold?

9 karat gold contains 9 parts gold out of 24 - or 37.5% pure gold. The remaining 62.5% is other metals, usually copper, silver and zinc.

It is the minimum gold content that can legally be sold as 'gold' in the UK and Australia. In India, however, BIS hallmarking covers only 14K (585), 18K (750) and 22K (916) - so 9K gold is not hallmarked under the Indian BIS system. You may not find a BIS mark on 9K pieces, but a '375' or '9K' stamp from the country of manufacture is the indicator.

What is 9K gold?

9K gold is 37.5% pure gold (375 hallmark). It is common in UK, Australian and European jewellery but not in Indian domestic production.

Is 9K gold real gold?

Yes - it contains 37.5% pure gold. It is a legitimate gold alloy, just with a lower gold content than Indian 22K or 18K jewellery.

What is the 375 stamp on gold?

Can I sell 9K gold in India?

9K gold is worth ₹5,719/g today. A 10g piece is ₹57,188.

Why is 9K gold not common in India?

Indian gold buyers and jewellers strongly prefer 22K (916) purity. 9K (37.5% gold) is considered too low a gold content for the Indian market.

Does the foreign hallmark affect the resale price in India?

No. XRF testing confirms the actual gold content regardless of hallmark origin. You are paid based on tested purity, not the stamped mark.

source.intent: Rate education: user checks gold rate on weekend/holiday, confused why it hasn't changed. Completely uncovered specific angle.

html:
You check the gold rate on a Sunday morning before deciding to sell and notice that the rate hasn't changed from Saturday. Or you visit a branch on a bank holiday and wonder whether the rate being used is current or stale.

This is one of the most common points of confusion for sellers. The answer is simple once you understand how India's gold rate publishing system works - and whether waiting until Monday changes anything.

At a Glance

IBJA rate published

Monday–Saturday on working days (2x daily)

Weekend rate

Last published Saturday rate applies

Holiday rate

Last working day rate applies

MCX futures

Closed on Sundays, some holidays

Does rate change over weekend?

Slightly - international markets move, but IBJA adjusts on next working day

Should you wait?

Usually no - weekend rate differences are minor

Last Updated

May 2026

Why the IBJA Rate Does Not Update on Weekends

The IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the gold rate on all MCX (Multi Commodity Exchange) working days - typically Monday through Saturday, excluding national holidays. The rate is published twice per day at approximately 11:30 AM and 5:00 PM.

On Sundays and declared MCX holidays, the IBJA does not publish. The rate that was last published on the preceding working day continues to apply until the next publication.

What Rate Applies When You Sell on a Weekend or Holiday?

  • The last officially published IBJA rate applies
  • The rate is publicly verifiable on ibja.co - you can confirm what the last published rate was
  • A reputable gold buyer will never use an artificially depressed rate on a holiday - the IBJA rate is the benchmark regardless of day

Does the Gold Price Actually Change Over a Weekend?

Technically, yes - the international gold spot price (London and New York) can move over a weekend due to global news, currency movements and trading in Asian markets that open on Sunday evening (IST).

However, the IBJA rate - which factors in customs duty and exchange rate - is only formally recalculated on the next working day. The practical effect on sellers is usually small. A weekend price movement of 0.5–1% is the typical range, and whether that moves up or down is impossible to predict.

Waiting until Monday to sell for a potentially better rate is a speculative decision - the rate could equally go up or down.

National Holidays When IBJA Does Not Publish

  • Republic Day (26 January)
  • Independence Day (15 August)
  • Gandhi Jayanti (2 October)
  • Dussehra / Navratri (varies)
  • Diwali / Lakshmi Puja (varies)
  • Holi (varies)
  • Christmas (25 December)
  • State-specific holidays may also apply
  • Check ibja.co for the current holiday list - it is published annually

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the gold rate today if it's a Sunday?

Does the gold rate change on bank holidays?

The IBJA does not publish a new rate on bank holidays. The previous working day's rate is used. International prices may move slightly but the Indian benchmark is only updated on the next working day.

Should I wait until Monday to sell gold?

Not necessarily. Weekend price movements are usually small and unpredictable - they could go up or down. Unless you have a specific reason to believe prices will rise significantly, waiting for Monday adds uncertainty without guaranteed benefit.

How do I check the last published IBJA rate?

Visit ibja.co - the official IBJA website - which shows the most recently published rates including the date and time of publication.

Is the gold rate the same across all cities on a holiday?

Yes - the IBJA publishes one national rate. Whether it is a working day or holiday, all cities use the same rate.

Why was the gold rate the same yesterday and today?

If both days were non-MCX working days (weekend/holiday), the rate from the last working day holds. This is normal and not a cause for concern.

More than 5% below IBJA without explanation

Refining cost, operating cost, buyer profit margin

Last Updated

Why Every Buyer Pays Below the IBJA Rate

The IBJA rate is the wholesale benchmark - equivalent to a stock's market price, not the price a broker charges retail investors. When a gold buyer purchases your jewellery, they must cover testing, branch operations, refinery processing and earn a margin. These costs are covered by the gap between IBJA and what they pay you. This is normal and universal.

Why Jewellers Often Pay Less Than Dedicated Buyers

  • Jewellers buy gold primarily as raw material for new jewellery - their buying price reflects manufacturing cost, not wholesale market
  • A dedicated buyer's model depends on high volume and small margins - jewellers take larger margins on fewer transactions
  • Always compare: visit a dedicated gold buyer and a jeweller - the difference is often 3–7%

How to Verify You Are Getting a Fair Rate

  1. Step 1: Check the IBJA rate on ibja.co. Today's 22K: ₹13,965/g
  2. Step 2: Calculate your gold's value: Weight × Purity fraction × IBJA rate
  3. Step 3: Ask any buyer: 'What rate per gram are you paying for 22K today?'
  4. Step 4: If the gap exceeds 3–4%, ask why - or visit another buyer
  5. Step 5: Ask to see the XRF reading - a transparent buyer shows you the purity result

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does the jeweller pay less than IBJA?

Every buyer deducts a margin for refining, operating costs and profit. 1–3% below IBJA is fair.

What is the IBJA gold rate?

The IBJA publishes the national benchmark gold rate twice daily on working days. It is India's standard.

How much below IBJA should I accept?

1–2% is standard. 3–4% is marginal. More than 5% without explanation is a red flag.

Can I negotiate the rate?

Yes - especially at smaller or independent buyers.

Where do I check the IBJA rate?

ibja.co - the official IBJA website, published twice on working days.

Is the rate different in different cities?

No - one national IBJA rate applies everywhere.

If you follow the gold rate in India closely, you will notice it sometimes rises even when international gold prices are flat. The reason is often the USD/INR exchange rate.

Understanding this relationship is not just academic - it helps you make smarter decisions about when to sell your gold.

At a Glance

Gold priced internationally in

US Dollars (USD) per troy ounce

IBJA converts to

INR per gram using live USD/INR rate

When rupee weakens

INR gold price rises even if USD price stays flat

When rupee strengthens

INR gold price falls even if USD price stays flat

When dollar falls globally

Gold typically rises in USD - both effects boost INR price

Last Updated

May 2026

Why Gold Is Priced in USD Globally

Gold is traded internationally in US Dollars on the LBMA (London) and COMEX (New York). The IBJA converts this to INR per gram using the live USD/INR rate, then adds import duty (15%). This means India's gold price is influenced by two factors: the global USD price of gold, and the USD/INR exchange rate.

What This Means for Indian Gold Sellers

  • A weakening rupee is good for gold sellers - even if global gold is flat, your INR value rises
  • Historically, rupee tends to weaken during global uncertainty - which is also when gold USD prices rise, both factors help the seller
  • A strong rupee can partially offset a rising USD gold price
  • When the RBI intervenes to support the rupee, this can reduce INR gold price gains
  • The IBJA rate on ibja.co already reflects all these factors - no need to calculate separately

Should You Wait for a Better Exchange Rate?

Very difficult to time. The rupee/dollar rate and gold price move independently under dozens of global influences. If you need to sell, sell at today's known rate rather than speculating on exchange rate movements.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the gold rate rise today even though international gold fell?

The rupee likely weakened against the dollar - a weaker rupee pushes the INR gold price up even when the USD price falls.

Does the gold rate change with the dollar every minute?

International spot price changes continuously, but the IBJA rate is published twice per working day.

When is the best time to sell based on exchange rate?

When the rupee is weak relative to historical norms and global gold is elevated simultaneously.

How does RBI intervention affect gold prices?

RBI selling dollars to strengthen the rupee can reduce INR gold price gains.

Where can I check the USD/INR rate?

Economic Times, Moneycontrol, or the RBI website show live rates.

Does import duty affect the gold rate?

Yes - 15% customs duty is baked into the IBJA rate. Any budget change to duty immediately changes the rate.

If the dollar is falling globally, is it a good time to sell?

Often yes - falling dollar usually pushes USD gold higher. Combined, this tends to lift the Indian gold rate.

html:
Every Union Budget in India has the potential to move the gold rate - sometimes significantly. Import duty changes can add or remove thousands of rupees per gram from the IBJA price overnight.

This guide explains how Budget 2026 affected gold import duty, what changed in the gold rate as a result, and what it means for selling gold now.

At a Glance

Gold import duty (current)

15% customs duty + 3% AGIF cess

Effect of 1% duty cut

Approximately ₹150/g reduction in gold rate

Effect of 1% duty increase

Approximately ₹150/g increase in gold rate

Budget impact on IBJA rate

Immediate - adjusts on announcement day

Who benefits from duty cut?

Buyers - lower purchase price

Who benefits from duty hike?

Sellers - higher resale rate

Last Updated

May 2026

How Import Duty Builds Into the Gold Rate

India imports approximately 700–900 tonnes of gold annually. Because most gold is imported, the customs duty rate directly impacts domestic gold prices.

Formula (approximate): Indian gold price = (International USD spot × USD/INR rate) + 15% customs duty + 3% AGIF cess + handling costs

When duty changes by 1 percentage point, the Indian gold price moves by approximately ₹130–150/g on 22K gold.

The Budget 2025 Duty Cut - A Key Reference

In Union Budget 2025, the government cut gold import duty from 15% to 6% - a 9-percentage point reduction. This caused the domestic gold rate to fall by approximately ₹1,000–1,200/g almost immediately.

For buyers, this was excellent. For sellers who purchased gold before the cut, the value of holdings dropped in the short term. By Budget 2026, duty had stabilised at 15%. The current IBJA rate reflects this.

Budget Change Impact on Sellers

Should You Sell Before or After a Budget?

  • If a duty cut is expected: sell before the Budget - duty cuts reduce the gold rate
  • If a duty hike is expected: wait until after - increases push the rate up
  • In practice, budget leaks are unreliable and markets often price in expected changes early
  • For most sellers: sell at today's known rate rather than speculating on budget outcomes

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened to gold rates after Budget 2025?

Import duty was cut significantly, causing the domestic gold rate to drop by approximately ₹1,000/g immediately after announcement.

Does every Budget change the gold rate?

Only if import duty, GST or other direct gold-related taxes are modified.

How much does a 1% duty cut reduce the gold rate?

Approximately ₹130–150/g on 22K gold.

What is the current import duty on gold?

15% basic customs duty plus 3% AGIF cess as of May 2026.

How quickly does the rate change after a budget?

Within hours of the duty announcement.

Should I sell gold before or after Budget 2026?

Depends on whether a duty cut or hike is expected. If uncertain, sell at today's known rate.

When is Union Budget 2026 presented?

Typically 1 February by the Finance Minister. The gold rate adjusts same day if duty changes.

html:
Selling gold inherited after a parent or family member passes away involves emotional sensitivity and practical compliance. Many families are unsure whether they need special legal documents, how capital gains tax is calculated, and what the process looks like.

This guide covers every practical aspect - from documents actually needed at the branch, to how income tax treats inherited gold.

At a Glance

Special documents for inherited gold?

Death certificate helpful - not mandatory for sale

Legal heir certificate needed?

Not required at a gold buyer

Capital gains tax basis

Deceased parent's original purchase price

Holding period

Includes the period the deceased held the gold

LTCG rate

12.5% if total holding ≥ 24 months

PAN required?

Yes if sale > ₹2,00,000

Last Updated

May 2026

Do You Need Special Documents to Sell Inherited Gold?

Tax on Selling Inherited Gold

Key rules:
1. Cost of acquisition = the original price the deceased paid (or FMV on 1 April 2001 if purchased before that date)
2. Holding period = from when the deceased first acquired the gold - not the date of inheritance
3. If total period is 24+ months → 12.5% LTCG
4. Under 24 months → profit added to income at slab rate

Scenario

Tax Treatment

Gold held by deceased 5 years, you sell immediately

24+ months → 12.5% LTCG on gain

Gold held by deceased 1 year, you sell 6 months later

18 months → STCG at slab rate

Very old jewellery - purchase date unknown

FMV on 1 April 2001 used as cost basis

Practical Steps to Sell Inherited Gold

  1. Gather the gold pieces you wish to sell
  2. Bring your Aadhaar card and PAN card (if applicable)
  3. Bring the deceased's purchase receipt if available - helps establish cost basis for tax
  4. XRF testing + weighing: 10–15 minutes
  5. Payment - cash or bank transfer - same visit
  6. Keep the sale receipt for ITR filing
  7. Declare capital gain in your Income Tax Return for the year of sale

Splitting Inherited Gold Among Multiple Heirs

  • All heirs visit the branch together, or split the gold physically before visiting
  • One heir can sell all and distribute cash to siblings - keep receipts for everyone
  • For gold in a joint bank locker: bank's protocol governs removal - often all holders need to be present

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell inherited gold without the original bill?

Yes. XRF tests purity at the branch - no purchase bill needed for the sale itself.

Do I need a legal heir certificate to sell gold?

Not at a gold buyer. Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable) are sufficient.

How is capital gains tax calculated on inherited gold?

Gain = Sale price − deceased's original purchase price. If total holding period 24+ months → 12.5% LTCG.

What if I don't know when the deceased bought the gold?

Use the FMV on 1 April 2001 as cost basis. A chartered accountant can assist.

Can multiple heirs sell together in one visit?

Yes - all heirs visit together. Receipt is in the name of whoever completes KYC.

Does a death certificate need to be shown to sell inherited gold?

No. Required for bank lockers or legal formalities - not at a gold buyer.

Should I declare inherited gold in my ITR?

Not when you receive it. When you sell, declare the capital gain in your ITR under Schedule CG.

html:
Gold is frequently part of divorce settlements in India - as Stridhan (a woman's personal gold), jointly held assets, or court-ordered property division. Once a settlement is reached, many individuals want to sell the gold received.

This guide covers what documents you need at a gold buyer, how capital gains tax applies to divorce-settlement gold, and whether a court order is needed to sell.

At a Glance

Special documents needed at branch?

No - Aadhaar + PAN if > ₹2L only

Court order needed to sell?

Not at a gold buyer - personal transaction

Capital gains on divorce-settlement gold?

Yes - complex if Stridhan (see below)

Stridhan gold treatment

Personal property - original donor cost basis

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is Stridhan? Is It Taxable When Sold?

Stridhan is gold exclusively the wife's - received as gifts at marriage from parents, relatives or in-laws. When Stridhan is sold:
• Cost of acquisition = original purchase price paid by the giver (parent/family)
• Holding period = from when the giver originally acquired it
• If total period 24+ months → 12.5% LTCG on the gain

For very old Stridhan where the original purchase date is unknown, the FMV on 1 April 2001 can be used as cost basis.

Gold Received as Part of Court-Ordered Divorce Settlement

If a court orders gold transfer as part of a divorce decree:
• The transfer itself at time of divorce is generally not taxable (court-ordered)
• When subsequently sold: capital gains apply based on the original buyer's purchase price and date
• This can result in a significant capital gain if gold has appreciated substantially

Selling Process at the Branch

  • Bring your Aadhaar (mandatory) and PAN (if > ₹2L)
  • No court order, divorce decree or consent from the other party required at the branch
  • XRF + weighing → offer → same-day payment
  • Keep the sale receipt for ITR - you'll need to declare the capital gain

Practical Advice

  • Separate only the gold you are entitled to before visiting
  • If gold is in a joint bank locker, you may need both parties present to remove it - bank requirement, not gold buyer requirement
  • Keep your divorce decree copy for records - may be needed if the capital gain is queried
  • Consult a CA for cost basis calculation, especially for Stridhan with unknown purchase dates

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to show divorce papers to sell gold?

No - Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable) are all that's required at the branch.

Is gold from a divorce settlement taxable?

When you sell it, yes - capital gains tax based on the original purchase price and date.

What is Stridhan and is it taxed when sold?

Stridhan is a woman's personal gold. Capital gains are calculated from the original gift/purchase date.

Can I sell gold that was jointly held before the divorce?

Yes, if awarded to you in the settlement.

What if the gold is in a joint bank locker?

Follow the bank's procedure for locker access - separate from the gold selling process.

How do I calculate the capital gain?

Sale price − original purchase price (of original buyer). Holding includes the original buyer's period.

Can I sell divorce-settlement gold the same day?

html:
Gold in India is frequently owned jointly - by spouses, parents and children, or siblings. When selling jointly held gold, questions arise: does both parties' consent need to be recorded? Who signs the receipt? What if one owner is abroad?

The answer depends on how the gold is held - physically at home, in a joint bank locker, or as a financial instrument.

At a Glance

Gold kept physically at home

Person physically selling it signs the receipt

Joint bank locker gold

Bank protocols apply - often both holders needed to remove

Gold in joint demat

Demat instructions usually require joint consent

Tax implications

Each owner reports their share of capital gain

One owner abroad?

Power of attorney or physical presence options

Last Updated

May 2026

Scenario 1: Gold Physically Kept at Home

For gold jewellery, coins or biscuits kept at home, the person who brings the gold to the branch and provides their Aadhaar is the seller on the receipt. A gold buyer does not verify joint ownership of physical gold - the legal division of proceeds between owners is between the parties, not the buyer.

Scenario 2: Gold in a Joint Bank Locker

Most banks require both locker holders present to open a joint locker, unless an 'either or survivor' clause was set up at the time of opening. If one holder is deceased, the bank requires a death certificate and succession documents per their policy.

Once the gold is physically removed from the locker, the gold buyer transaction is standard - Aadhaar + PAN.

Scenario 3: One Owner Is Abroad or Unavailable

  • Power of Attorney (POA): the absent owner can give a registered POA authorising the present owner to act for the gold sale
  • For physical gold at home: the person present can sell it - but the absent owner retains legal rights to their share of proceeds
  • For locker gold: the bank's rules govern access - check with your specific bank
  • If the absent person does not consent: do not sell their portion of jointly owned gold without consent

Tax: How Joint Gold Capital Gains Are Reported

If both owners are on record as holding the gold, each owner reports their proportionate share of the capital gain in their respective ITR. If only one owner's Aadhaar is on the receipt, that owner reports the full capital gain in their ITR and transfers the other party's share separately.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does my spouse need to come to the branch when I sell our gold?

For physical gold at home, no. For joint bank locker gold, your bank's procedures govern.

Can I sell gold from a joint locker alone?

Only if your locker agreement has an 'either or survivor' clause. Check with your bank.

Who pays capital gains tax on jointly held gold?

Each owner reports their share proportionally. If only one person's name is on the receipt, that person reports the full gain.

What if my co-owner is deceased?

For physical gold, the living owner can sell with standard documents. For locker gold, bank requires death certificate and succession documentation.

Can I use a Power of Attorney to sell on behalf of a joint owner?

Yes - a registered POA authorising the gold sale can be used.

What if joint owners disagree on whether to sell?

A gold buyer cannot adjudicate ownership disputes. Both owners need to agree before selling.

Is the sale receipt in one name or both?

In the name of the person presenting their Aadhaar at the branch.

keywords.keyword: sell gold on behalf of child

html:
Gold is frequently gifted to children in India - at birth, naming ceremonies, religious occasions and school milestones. By adulthood, a child may hold significant gold from family gifts.

Can a minor (under 18) sell gold themselves? And if a parent sells on behalf of a minor, what are the rules?

At a Glance

Legal age to contract in India

18 years

Can a minor sell gold alone?

No - contract with minor is void under Indian law

Who can sell for a minor?

Natural guardian (parent) or court-appointed guardian

Documents needed

Guardian Aadhaar + minor birth certificate or school ID

Tax on minor gold sale?

Clubbed with guardian income under Section 64(1A)

Last Updated

May 2026

Legal Position: Minors Cannot Enter Contracts

Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract with a minor is void ab initio. Selling gold is a contract - therefore a person under 18 cannot legally sell gold on their own. The natural guardian (parent or legal guardian) must conduct the sale on the minor's behalf. The gold buyer records the guardian's Aadhaar - not the minor's.

Process: Selling Gold Owned by a Minor

  1. Natural guardian (parent) brings the minor's gold to the branch
  2. Guardian presents their own Aadhaar card
  3. Guardian presents PAN if sale > ₹2,00,000
  4. Minor's birth certificate or school ID may be asked to confirm relationship
  5. Receipt is issued in the guardian's name as legal representative
  6. Proceeds belong to the minor - guardian holds them in trust
  7. Capital gain is reported in the guardian's ITR (clubbed with their income)

Tax Treatment: Minor Gold Sale

Under Section 64(1A) of the Income Tax Act, a minor's income is clubbed with the parent with higher income. This applies to capital gains from selling the minor's gold:
• Capital gain added to the higher-earning parent's taxable income
• Parent may claim ₹1,500/minor/year exemption
• Holding period uses the original gift date

When a Minor Turns 18

At 18, they can independently sell their gold. They will need their own Aadhaar and PAN (if sale > ₹2L). The transaction proceeds like any adult seller's.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a 16-year-old sell gold?

No - under 18 cannot legally enter a sale contract. The natural guardian must sell on their behalf.

What documents are needed to sell a minor's gold?

Guardian's Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable). Minor's birth certificate or school ID may be requested.

Who receives the money when a minor's gold is sold?

Legally, the proceeds belong to the minor. The guardian holds them in trust for the minor's benefit.

Is the capital gain on a minor's gold sale taxable?

Yes - clubbed with the higher-earning parent's income under Section 64(1A).

Can grandparents sell gold gifted to a minor grandchild?

Only if they are the court-appointed or natural guardian of the minor.

When can a child sell their own gold independently?

From age 18 - once legally an adult and able to enter contracts.

Can a minor have a PAN card?

Yes - applied through the guardian. But for gold sales, the guardian's PAN is typically used.

What If the Gold Exceeds the CBDT Limits?

For most families selling ancestral jewellery: the amount is typically within limits, and a reasonable family inheritance narrative is generally accepted.

html:
In India, gold gifted at weddings is one of the most significant sources of gold ownership. Families gift sovereigns, jewellery sets, biscuits and coins - and the recipient may hold this gold for years before deciding to sell.

The key question when selling wedding gift gold: how is it taxed? The answer differs from gold you purchased - the donor's purchase price and date become the basis for your capital gains.

At a Glance

Gift tax on wedding gifts?

No - gifts from relatives at marriage are tax-exempt

Capital gains when you sell?

Yes - based on donor original price and purchase date

Holding period

Includes the donor holding period before gifting

LTCG rate

12.5% if total period ≥ 24 months

Cost basis

Donor original purchase price

Documents at branch

Aadhaar + PAN if sale > ₹2L

Last Updated

May 2026

Is Wedding Gift Gold Taxable When Received?

Under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act, gifts from specified relatives are tax-exempt regardless of value. Relatives include parents, siblings, in-laws, grandparents. Gold gifts received on the occasion of marriage are also exempt - even from non-relatives for the recipient's wedding. So: the gold received as a wedding gift is not taxable when you receive it.

Capital Gains When You Sell Wedding Gift Gold

Even though the gift is not taxable, selling it later triggers capital gains:
1. Cost of acquisition = the price the donor originally paid
2. Holding period = from when the donor originally bought the gold (not from when gifted to you)
3. If total period 24+ months → 12.5% LTCG on the gain

Example: Parents bought 50g in 2015 for ₹3,00,000. Gifted at your 2019 wedding. You sell today for ₹7,00,000.
Capital gain = ₹7,00,000 − ₹3,00,000 = ₹4,00,000
Holding period: 2015–2026 = 11 years → LTCG
Tax: ₹4,00,000 × 12.5% = ₹50,000

Step

What It Means for Wedding Gift Gold

Cost basis

Donor original purchase price - not market value at time of gift

Holding period start

Date the donor originally bought the gold

24-month rule

Almost always met for wedding gifts (donors buy years before gifting)

Tax rate

12.5% LTCG (typically)

Where to find cost basis

Donor original purchase receipt or jewellery bill

What If You Don't Have the Donor's Original Receipt?

  • For very old gold (pre-2001): use FMV on 1 April 2001 as cost basis
  • For gold where purchase year is known but not exact price: approximate rate from that year's records
  • A chartered accountant can help reconstruct a reasonable cost basis
  • Income tax department generally accepts reasonable estimates for old ancestral gold

Selling Process

  • Bring Aadhaar and PAN (if sale > ₹2L)
  • No wedding invitation, gift certificate or donor bill needed at the branch
  • Keep the sale receipt for ITR filing
  • Keep the donor's original purchase bill if you have it - needed for cost basis in ITR

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold received as a wedding gift taxable?

When received, no - wedding gifts from relatives are exempt. When you sell it, capital gains apply based on the donor original price.

What is the capital gains rate on wedding gift gold?

12.5% LTCG if total holding period (including donor period) is 24+ months.

Do I need wedding records at the branch?

No - Aadhaar and PAN only. Wedding records are for your own tax filing.

What if I don't know the original price my parents paid?

Use FMV on 1 April 2001. A CA can help for more recent purchases.

Can I sell gold gifted by in-laws after marriage?

Yes. Gold gifts from in-laws at marriage are also exempt. Capital gains based on in-laws original purchase price.

What if the donor has passed away?

Same rules apply - use the deceased donor original price as cost basis. If unavailable, use FMV on 1 April 2001.

Do I need to report the wedding gift in my ITR?

Not when received - exempt. Only when sold do you report the capital gain under Schedule CG.

This guide explains exactly why dedicated gold buyers typically pay more than jewellers, and what to check to get the best rate either way.

html:
Making charges typically add 8–25% to the cost of gold jewellery - and none of it is recovered when you sell. Reducing making charges at purchase is the single most impactful way to improve your gold investment's resale efficiency.

Can you actually negotiate making charges? Yes - in many cases, significantly. Here is how.

At a Glance

Making charges typical range

8% – 25% of gold value

Most negotiable

Independent and local jewellers

Least negotiable

Large chains during peak festival seasons

Best time to negotiate

Off-season, large purchases, cash payment

Maximum realistic saving

3% – 10% reduction from quoted charges

Biggest lever

Buying a larger quantity at once

Last Updated

May 2026

Step 1: Always Ask for Per-Gram Making Charges

Never ask 'what is your making charge?' in percentage terms - the answer is hard to verify. Ask: 'What is the making charge per gram on this specific piece?' This forces a concrete, comparable answer. Typical range: ₹150–800/g for hand-crafted pieces, ₹80–250/g for machine-made.

Step 2: Get Three Quotes First

Visit three jewellers before committing. Real competitor quotes are the most powerful negotiating tool: 'Jeweller B is offering this at ₹200/g making charges. Can you match or beat that?'

Step 3: Know When Jewellers Are Most Flexible

  • Off-season months (February–March, June–August) - lower footfall, more flexibility
  • Large purchases - ₹5L+ gives significant bargaining leverage
  • Slow-moving designs - pieces in display for months are more negotiable
  • Cash or UPI payment - eliminates the jeweller card fee (1.5–2%), which they may share with you
  • End of financial year (March) - jewellers clearing old stock
  • 6+ months advance for wedding orders - time and value both create leverage

Step 4: Separate Wastage from Making Charges

Some jewellers combine wastage (3–5%) with making charges (8–12%) - a combined quote hides the negotiable part. Ask: 'Can you show me the wastage and making charges separately?' Wastage is less negotiable (actual manufacturing loss); making charges have a profit component.

Step 5: What You Cannot Negotiate Away

  • GST on making charges (5%) - statutory, not the jeweller's to waive
  • BIS hallmarking cost - minor but fixed
  • The gold value itself (IBJA rate + buy premium) - market-set
  • Machine-made basics (chains, plain bangles) - often already at minimum 8–10%

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you negotiate making charges with Tanishq or Malabar?

Large chains have less flexibility during peak seasons. Off-season, for large purchases, some reduction is possible. Independent jewellers offer much more room.

How much can I realistically reduce making charges?

3–10% reduction from the initial quote is common for experienced negotiators on off-season purchases.

Is it rude to negotiate making charges?

Not at all. Gold is a major purchase in India - bargaining is expected and respected.

Does negotiating making charges affect gold quality?

No - making charges and gold purity are completely separate.

What is the minimum making charge on gold jewellery?

Machine-made plain jewellery can be as low as 6–8%. Handcrafted or designer pieces rarely go below 12–15%.

Can I negotiate for a wedding order?

Yes - wedding orders are large-value and planned well in advance. Place the order 3–6 months before the wedding and negotiate hard.

Should I ask for zero making charges?

Very rarely achievable. Some jewellers offer it as a promotional event, but the gold rate offered may be slightly adjusted. Always calculate the total cost.

html:
Every gold seller in India is told: 'Check the IBJA rate before you sell.' But for first-time sellers, ibja.co can be confusing - multiple rows, different purity levels, AM and PM columns, and rates that differ slightly from news apps.

This step-by-step guide shows you exactly how to read the IBJA rate table, which row applies to your gold, and how to convert the per-gram rate into what your specific piece is worth.

At a Glance

IBJA stands for

India Bullion and Jewellers Association

Website

ibja.co

Published

Twice daily - ~11:30 AM and ~5:00 PM (working days)

What it shows

Rate per 10g for multiple purities (995, 916, 750 etc.)

Convert to per gram

Divide the shown rate by 10

Most relevant row for jewellery

916 (22K) - Indian jewellery standard

Last Updated

May 2026

Step 1: Go to ibja.co

Open ibja.co in your browser - this is the official IBJA website. Alternatively, Moneycontrol or Economic Times publish the IBJA rate daily. For the authoritative source, ibja.co is primary.

Step 2: Find the Most Recent Rate Publication

The IBJA rate is published twice per working day:
• First publication: approximately 11:30 AM
• Second publication: approximately 5:00 PM

The website shows the date and time of the most recent publication. On weekends or holidays, the last published rate from the previous working day is displayed - this is the applicable rate.

Step 3: Read the Rate Table

The IBJA table shows rates per 10 grams for multiple purities. Key rows:

Step 4: Calculate What Your Gold Is Worth

Formula: Weight (g) × IBJA per-gram rate for your purity

Examples with today's rates:
• 15g of 22K: 15 × ₹13,965 = ₹2,09,535
• 25g of 22K: 25 × ₹13,965 = ₹3,49,225
• 10g of 18K: 10 × ₹11,438 = ₹1,14,375
• 8g sovereign (22K): 8 × ₹13,965 = ₹1,11,752

This is the reference figure to walk in with. A reputable buyer offers within 1–2% of this.

Step 5: Verify the Buyer's Offer

  • Ask: 'What rate per gram are you paying for 22K today?' Today's IBJA: ₹13,965/g
  • Calculate the gap: if they offer ₹13,546/g, that is a 3% discount from IBJA - acceptable but on the high end
  • If they cannot state their rate in per-gram terms - or refuse to - that is a red flag
  • Ask to see the XRF reading after testing - confirm it matches what they are paying against

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the IBJA gold rate?

The IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association) gold rate is India's national benchmark, published twice daily on working days.

How do I check today's gold rate?

Visit ibja.co or check Moneycontrol/Economic Times. For the official source, ibja.co is primary.

Why does my gold buyer quote below the IBJA rate?

Buyers pay slightly below IBJA (1–3%) to cover operating costs and margin. IBJA is the wholesale benchmark, not a retail buying rate.

Is the IBJA rate different for different cities?

No - one national rate applies everywhere.

Why does the IBJA show rates per 10 grams?

Historical convention - gold was quoted per 10g in India. Divide by 10 for the per-gram rate.

What does AM and PM rate mean on ibja.co?

IBJA publishes two rates per working day - morning (~11:30 AM) and evening (~5:00 PM). The more recent publication is current.

Can I use the IBJA rate to verify any gold buyer?

Yes - it is the standard benchmark all reputable buyers in India use as their pricing reference.

html:
BIS hallmarking became mandatory for Indian jewellers only from June 2021. This means most gold bought before 2021 - and virtually all gold bought before 2000 - is not BIS hallmarked.

Does this mean you get less for it when you sell? No - but the purity must be determined differently. Here is exactly how unhallmarked gold is valued and what to expect.

At a Glance

BIS mandatory hallmarking from

June 2021 (14K, 18K, 22K jewellery)

Pre-2021 jewellery

Not hallmarked - but completely sellable

How purity is determined

XRF testing - same as any gold

Rate for unhallmarked 22K

₹13,965/g - same as hallmarked 22K if XRF confirms

Does no hallmark reduce value?

No - XRF result determines rate, not the stamp

Last Updated

May 2026

Why Most Old Indian Jewellery Has No BIS Hallmark

BIS hallmarking was introduced in 2000 but was voluntary until June 2021. This means:
• Jewellery bought before June 2021 - no BIS hallmark required by law
• Family heirlooms, ancestral pieces, jewellery from small local jewellers - likely no hallmark
• None of this makes the jewellery less valuable - purity simply needs independent verification.

How Unhallmarked Gold Is Valued at Resale

Why Older Jewellery May Test Below Expected Purity

  • Old KDM jewellery (pre-2000, cadmium soldering) may have slightly lower purity near solder joints
  • Some older jewellers sold jewellery at lower purity than claimed - without mandatory hallmarking, there was no verification
  • Pieces repaired or altered with lower-purity gold may test lower overall
  • Lac and resin filling inside hollow pieces affects weight but not the purity of the gold itself
  • Family heirlooms repaired over generations may be a mix of purities

Does No Hallmark Mean Lower Payment?

No - provided XRF confirms the expected purity. A 22K piece testing at 91.6% gets the same rate as a BIS-hallmarked 916 piece: ₹13,965/g.

The hallmark is a pre-verified purity certification. XRF at the branch does the same job - in real time, in front of you.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold without a BIS hallmark?

Will I get less money for unhallmarked gold?

No - if XRF confirms the expected purity, you receive the same rate as hallmarked gold of that purity.

How is purity determined for old unhallmarked jewellery?

XRF (X-ray fluorescence) testing - non-destructive, identifies exact gold content in 30–60 seconds.

What if the XRF shows lower purity than I expected?

You are paid at the tested purity. If the piece tests at 18K when you assumed 22K, the 18K rate applies.

Is KDM gold (old cadmium solder) affected?

XRF tests the gold body, not the solder joint. The gold portion of a KDM piece is paid at its actual purity.

Should I get my old gold tested before visiting?

Does old ancestral gold always test lower?

Not necessarily. Old South Indian hand-crafted jewellery is often genuinely 22K or close to it.

source.title: Selling Dental Gold in India
source.intent: Educational: dental crowns/bridges are 10K–18K gold — many people unaware of resale value. XRF testing at branch. Completely uncovered.

html:
Gold has been used in dentistry for over a century - crowns, inlays, onlays and bridges are made from gold alloys because of their durability and biocompatibility. When a crown or bridge is removed during dental work, many people have no idea that the small metal piece has real cash value.

In India, dental gold can absolutely be sold to a gold buyer. Here is what it contains, how it is tested, and what you can realistically expect to receive.

At a Glance

Dental gold purity range

10K – 18K (375–750) depending on type and era

Modern dental gold crowns

Often 10K–14K - 40–60% gold

Older dental gold (pre-1990s)

Sometimes higher purity (16K–18K)

Typical weight per crown

1g – 3g per crown or inlay

Tested by

XRF - same as jewellery

Cash value per crown

Approx ₹8,921 – ₹34,312 depending on purity and weight

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is Dental Gold Made Of?

Dental gold is not 22K or 24K - it is an alloy designed for durability and biocompatibility. Common types:
• High-noble dental gold: 60%+ gold (≈14K–18K) + palladium, platinum - most valuable
• Noble dental gold: 25–60% gold (≈6K–14K) + silver, copper
• Base metal dental alloys: Less than 25% gold - some barely qualify
• Porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crowns: Metal base may be very low gold or none at all

XRF testing immediately identifies the actual gold content.

How Much Is a Gold Crown Worth?

Crown Type

Typical Purity

  1. Clean them - remove visible residue, no polishing needed
  2. XRF testing identifies the gold percentage
  3. Pieces weighed on precision digital scale
  4. Payout = Weight × Purity fraction × IBJA rate
  5. Payment - cash or bank transfer - same visit
  6. Documents: Aadhaar mandatory, PAN if sale > ₹2,00,000

Palladium and Platinum in Dental Gold

High-noble dental alloys often contain palladium and sometimes platinum alongside gold. At a standard gold buyer, only gold content is typically valued - palladium and platinum are not separately extracted.

For very large quantities of high-noble dental gold, a specialist precious metals refiner may offer a better total return by assaying all precious metals separately. For individual crowns and bridges, this extra complexity is rarely worth it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell old gold dental crowns in India?

How much is a gold crown worth?

Typically ₹8,921–₹34,312 depending on purity (10K–18K) and weight (1–3g per crown). XRF testing at the branch gives the exact figure.

How do I know if my crown is gold or porcelain?

Gold crowns are metallic - gold-coloured or silver/white metal. Porcelain or ceramic crowns are tooth-coloured. If unsure, XRF testing confirms immediately.

Do I need to clean dental gold before selling?

Remove visible residue. No polishing is needed - branch staff handle the rest.

What is the purity of dental gold?

Modern dental gold is typically 10K–18K. Older pieces (pre-1990) may be higher. XRF confirms the exact percentage.

Is palladium in dental gold paid for separately?

At a standard gold buyer, typically no - only gold content is paid. For large quantities, consider a specialist precious metals refiner.

Documents needed to sell dental gold?

Same as any gold sale: Aadhaar (mandatory) and PAN (if sale > ₹2,00,000).

metaTitle: Gold Filled Jewellery India | What It Is & Resale Value Explained
description: Gold-filled jewellery is one of the most confusing categories in the jewellery market. The name suggests solid gold - but it is not. It is a base metal (usually brass) bonded with a…

source.title: What Is Gold-Filled Jewellery?
source.intent: Educational: user has gold-filled piece — wants to know value. Zero coverage in existing blogs.

html:
Gold-filled jewellery is one of the most confusing categories in the jewellery market. The name suggests solid gold - but it is not. It is a base metal (usually brass) bonded with a thick layer of gold alloy under heat and pressure.

If you have gold-filled pieces and are wondering what they are worth when you sell them, this guide gives you the honest answer.

At a Glance

What is gold-filled?

Base metal bonded with a thick gold layer - not solid gold

Gold content

5% of total weight by US FTC standards (1/20th gold)

Common stamps

GF, 1/20 14K GF, 12K GF, 1/20 12K

Resale value

Very low - typically not accepted at gold buyer rates

Difference from gold plated

Thicker gold layer - more durable but still not solid

Difference from solid gold

Solid gold is 100% gold alloy throughout

Last Updated

May 2026

Gold-Filled vs Gold Plated vs Solid Gold

Type

Gold Content

Durability

Resale Value at Gold Buyer

Solid 22K gold

91.6% throughout

Lifetime

Full IBJA rate

Solid 18K gold

75% throughout

Lifetime

Full IBJA rate

Gold-filled

~5% of total weight (gold layer only)

5–30 years

Very low - base metal dominates

Gold plated

0.05–0.5% of weight

1–5 years

Nil - gold layer negligible

Gold vermeil

~5% (sterling silver base)

5–20 years

Silver scrap value only

Can You Sell Gold-Filled Jewellery at a Gold Buyer?

XRF testing immediately identifies gold-filled pieces - the gold layer is visible but the base metal underneath shows through. Because the gold content is only about 5% of the total weight, the gold value in a typical 10g gold-filled piece is only about 0.5g of gold - worth approximately ₹4,461 at 14K rates.

Most dedicated gold buyers either do not accept gold-filled pieces or pay only scrap rates. The payout is extremely low compared to solid gold of the same weight and appearance.

How to Identify Gold-Filled Jewellery

  • Look for the stamp: 'GF', '1/20 14K GF', '12K GF' or '1/20 12K' - these indicate gold-filled
  • Gold-filled is significantly heavier per piece than gold plated (base metal adds weight)
  • The gold layer on gold-filled is thick enough to survive XRF - it shows the gold layer clearly but the base metal underneath is also detected
  • If the piece has no hallmark, XRF testing will determine whether it is solid gold or gold-filled
  • Gold-filled pieces made in the USA often have GF stamps; European pieces may have different marking systems

What to Do If You Have Gold-Filled Pieces

  • XRF test it first - confirm whether it is gold-filled or solid gold (they can look identical)
  • If gold-filled: the resale value at a gold buyer will be minimal
  • Consider keeping it as wearable jewellery if it is in good condition
  • Some antique dealers value vintage gold-filled pieces for their aesthetics
  • Do not assume it is worthless - bring it for XRF testing and let the result determine the value

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold-filled jewellery real gold?

It contains real gold - but only as a surface layer (about 5% of total weight). The core is brass or another base metal. It is not solid gold.

What is the resale value of gold-filled jewellery?

Very low. The gold content per gram is minimal. A 10g piece may yield only 0.3–0.5g of gold value.

How do I know if my jewellery is gold-filled?

Is gold-filled better than gold plated?

Yes - gold-filled has a much thicker gold layer (100x or more than gold plating) and is far more durable. But neither is solid gold.

XRF testing will identify it accurately. Payouts for gold-filled pieces are very low because the gold content is minimal.

What is the GF stamp on jewellery?

GF stands for Gold-Filled. A stamp like 1/20 14K GF means the gold layer is 14K gold and represents 1/20th (5%) of the total weight.

Does gold-filled jewellery tarnish?

The gold layer does not tarnish. However, at cut edges or worn areas, the base metal underneath may show through over time.

It is often sold as a premium alternative to gold plating - but it is important to understand exactly what it is before assuming it has resale value like solid gold.

What Vermeil Is Worth at Resale

Because the gold layer in vermeil is extremely thin (measured in microns), the actual gold content is negligible - less than 0.01g for most pieces. The valuable metal in vermeil is the silver base.

A 10g vermeil piece is essentially a 10g sterling silver piece with gold cosmetics:
• Silver value (92.5% = 9.25g fine silver): approximately ₹694 at current silver prices (~₹75/g)
• Gold layer: too thin to recover economically

At a gold buyer, vermeil is typically not purchased at the gold rate. If it is purchased at all, it is as silver scrap.

How to Identify Vermeil

  • Stamps: '925 Gold Vermeil', '925 14K' or just '925' (sterling silver hallmark) with a gold appearance
  • Lighter than solid gold of the same visual size
  • Often used in designer fashion jewellery, online marketplace jewellery

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold vermeil real gold?

It has a real gold coating but the base is sterling silver. It is not solid gold throughout.

What is the resale value of gold vermeil?

Minimal - only the sterling silver base has meaningful scrap value. The gold layer is too thin to recover economically.

XRF testing will confirm it is vermeil. If purchased, it would be valued as silver - not at the gold rate.

How is vermeil different from gold plated?

Vermeil has a thicker gold layer (2.5+ microns vs 0.05 microns) and uses sterling silver as the base instead of brass.

What stamp does vermeil have?

Usually 925 (for sterling silver) with a gold appearance. Sometimes labeled 'Gold Vermeil' explicitly.

Is vermeil a good investment?

No - the resale value is essentially silver scrap. Vermeil is a fashion jewellery choice, not an investment.

How long does gold vermeil last?

2–5 years of daily wear before the gold layer shows wear through. Much longer if worn occasionally.

html:
'Gold over silver' or 'GOS' is a marking you might find on imported jewellery - it simply means a silver base metal with a gold layer applied on top. It is essentially the same as gold vermeil in construction, though the term is more commonly used in American and European jewellery markets.

If you own a piece marked GOS and want to know its resale value, this guide explains what you are dealing with.

At a Glance

Gold over silver means

Silver base with gold layer - not solid gold

Common stamp

GOS, 925 GOS, or Gold over Silver

Gold content

Very thin gold layer over silver core

Resale value

Silver scrap value - gold layer negligible

Same as vermeil?

Essentially yes - silver base, gold plating

Last Updated

May 2026

What Does GOS Mean on Jewellery?

GOS stands for 'Gold Over Silver'. It indicates that the piece is made of sterling silver (92.5% silver) as the base, with gold electroplated or bonded on the surface.

Common stamps include:
• GOS
• 925 GOS
• Gold Over Silver
• Sterling Silver with Gold

In practical terms, GOS is interchangeable with gold vermeil - both are silver pieces with a gold coating.

Resale Value of Gold Over Silver

At a gold buyer, GOS pieces are valued for their silver content - not the gold layer. The gold coating is too thin to have meaningful gold recovery value.

For a 10g GOS piece:
• Silver value (92.5% = 9.25g fine silver) at ~₹75/g = approximately ₹694
• Gold layer: negligible

Compare this to a 10g solid 22K piece which is worth ₹1,39,690 - more than 100x the value of the GOS piece.

How to Distinguish GOS from Solid Gold

  • Stamp: GOS pieces are typically stamped 925 (sterling silver purity) alongside the GOS marking
  • Weight: silver is denser than gold per apparent volume for large pieces - but this is hard to judge visually
  • Magnet test: silver and gold are both non-magnetic, so this does not differentiate
  • XRF testing: the definitive test - shows silver core and thin gold layer immediately
  • Acid test: will show silver reaction at any exposed edge
  • Hallmark: solid gold pieces will have 916, 750, or 585 BIS stamps - GOS will have 925

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold over silver real gold?

It has a real gold coating, but the core is sterling silver. It is not solid gold throughout - the gold layer is very thin.

What is GOS on jewellery?

GOS stands for Gold Over Silver - a sterling silver piece with a gold layer on the surface.

What is the resale value of gold over silver jewellery?

Essentially silver scrap value. The gold layer is too thin to recover economically at a standard gold buyer.

Is GOS the same as gold vermeil?

Yes - essentially. Both are sterling silver with a gold layer. GOS is the American term; vermeil is the French/European term.

XRF testing will confirm it as silver with a gold coating. It would be valued as silver scrap, not gold.

How do I know if my piece is GOS or solid gold?

Look for the stamp: solid gold has 916, 750, or 585. GOS has 925 or GOS marking. XRF testing at the branch confirms definitively.

Does GOS jewellery tarnish?

The gold surface does not tarnish easily, but the silver base can tarnish at worn areas where the gold layer has thinned.

source.intent: Rate education: user confuses international spot price with IBJA rate. How import duty builds into Indian rate. Uncovered.

html:
If you check the gold price online, you will often see two different numbers: the 'spot price' in US dollars per troy ounce, and the IBJA rate in Indian rupees per gram. These two numbers are related but not the same - and confusing them can lead to significant miscalculations when you try to estimate what your gold is worth.

This guide explains both clearly.

At a Glance

Spot gold price

International price in USD per troy ounce (31.1g)

IBJA rate

Indian benchmark in INR per gram - what you use to sell

Difference

Spot + import duty + USD/INR conversion + handling = IBJA

Which to use when selling?

Always the IBJA rate - not the international spot price

Where to check IBJA

ibja.co - published twice daily on working days

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is the Spot Gold Price?

The spot gold price is the current price of gold in the international wholesale market - expressed in US Dollars per troy ounce. It is set continuously by trading on the LBMA (London Bullion Market Association) and COMEX (New York) futures exchange.

One troy ounce = 31.1035 grams.

If the international spot price is $2,400/oz, that equates to $2,400 ÷ 31.1 = approximately $77/g in USD.

How the IBJA Rate Is Derived from the Spot Price

The IBJA rate is not simply a direct conversion of the spot price. It adds several India-specific factors:

1. USD/INR exchange rate (live)
2. Basic customs duty: 15%
3. AGIF (Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess): 3%
4. Social Welfare Surcharge: ~10% on customs duty
5. Refining and handling margins

Result: Indian gold prices are systematically higher than the raw USD spot price would suggest after simple currency conversion. This is why India's gold price often seems high compared to international benchmarks - the import duty structure adds approximately 18–20% above the pure conversion rate.

Why You Should Use the IBJA Rate, Not the Spot Price

  • The spot price is for institutional wholesale gold - not the rate at which Indian buyers purchase or sell
  • The IBJA rate is the actual Indian benchmark that gold buyers use to pay sellers
  • If you convert the spot price directly to INR/g, you will underestimate the Indian gold price by 15–20%
  • Always use ibja.co for the correct Indian per-gram rate before going to sell
  • Financial news apps (Moneycontrol, ET Money) typically show the IBJA rate - but always verify the source

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the spot gold price today in India?

The spot price is an international USD figure. Use the IBJA rate (on ibja.co) for the Indian selling rate.

Why is India's gold price higher than the international spot price?

India adds approximately 18–20% in import duty, cess and handling costs to the international price.

Does the Indian gold rate always follow the international spot price?

Yes, directionally - when the international price rises, India's IBJA rate rises too. But the exact conversion includes duty and exchange rate factors.

Where can I check the real gold price for selling in India?

ibja.co for the official IBJA rate, published twice per working day.

If the international gold price falls, does India's gold price also fall?

Generally yes - but the magnitude depends on the USD/INR exchange rate and whether any duty changes occur.

What is a troy ounce?

A troy ounce is 31.1035 grams - the international standard unit for gold pricing. It is different from a standard (avoirdupois) ounce of 28.35g.

Is the IBJA rate the same as the spot gold price?

No - the IBJA rate is India's domestic benchmark derived from the international spot price after adding import duty, exchange rate conversion and other charges.
